children.text: śrī-ādi-nāthāya namo'stu tasmai
children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Śrī Ādinātha</s> (the Primordial Lord),

children.text: yenopadiṣṭā haṭha-yoga-vidyā /
children.translated_text: By whom the science of <s>Haṭha Yoga</s> was taught,

children.text: vibhrājate pronnata-rāja-yogam
children.translated_text: Which shines as a stairway for those

children.text: āroḍhum icchor adhirohiṇīva // HYP_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Who wish to ascend to the exalted <s>Rāja Yoga</s>. // HYP 1.1 //

children.text: praṇamya śrī-guruṃ nāthaṃ svātmārāmeṇa yoginā /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the revered <s>Guru</s> and Lord, by the <s>yogī</s> <s>Svātmārāma</s>,

children.text: kevalaṃ rāja-yogāya haṭha-vidyopadiśyate // HYP_1.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Haṭha Vidyā</s> (the science of Haṭha) is taught solely for the sake of <s>Rāja Yoga</s>. // HYP 1.2 //

children.text: bhrāntyā bahumata-dhvānte rāja-yogam ajānatām /
children.translated_text: For those who, in the darkness of many conflicting opinions due to confusion, do not know <s>Rāja Yoga</s>,

children.text: haṭha-pradīpikāṃ dhatte svātmārāmaḥ kṛpākaraḥ // HYP_1.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Svātmārāma</s>, the compassionate one, offers this <s>Haṭha Pradīpikā</s> (Light on Haṭha). // HYP 1.3 //

children.text: haṭha-vidyāṃ hi matsyendra-gorakṣādyā vijānate /
children.translated_text: The science of <s>Haṭha</s> is known to <s>Matsyendra</s>, <s>Gorakṣa</s>, and others;

children.text: svātmārāmo'thavā yogī jānīte tat-prasādataḥ // HYP_1.4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> <s>Svātmārāma</s> knows it by their grace. // HYP 1.4 //

children.text: śrī-ādinātha-matsyendra-śāvarānanda-bhairavāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Ādinātha</s>, <s>Matsyendra</s>, <s>Śāvara</s>, <s>Ānanda Bhairava</s>,

children.text: cauraṅgī-mīna-gorakṣa-virūpākṣa-bileśayāḥ // HYP_1.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cauraṅgī</s>, <s>Mīna</s>, <s>Gorakṣa</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Bileśaya</s>, // HYP 1.5 //

children.text: manthāno bhairavo yogī siddhir buddhaś ca kanthaḍiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Manthāna</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Yogī Siddhi</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, and <s>Kanthaḍi</s>,

children.text: koraṃṭakaḥ surānandaḥ siddhapādaś ca carpaṭiḥ // HYP_1.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Koraṃṭaka</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Siddhapāda</s>, and <s>Carpaṭi</s>, // HYP 1.6 //

children.text: kānerī pūjyapādaś ca nitya-nātho nirañjanaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānerī</s>, <s>Pūjyapāda</s>, <s>Nityanātha</s>, <s>Nirañjana</s>,

children.text: kapālī bindunāthaś ca kākacaṇḍīśvarāhvayaḥ // HYP_1.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Bindunātha</s>, and the one called <s>Kākacaṇḍīśvara</s>, // HYP 1.7 //

children.text: allāmaḥ prabhudevaś ca ghoḍā colī ca ṭiṃṭiṇiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Allāma</s>, <s>Prabhudeva</s>, <s>Ghoḍā</s>, <s>Colī</s>, and <s>Ṭiṃṭiṇi</s>,

children.text: bhānukī nāradevaś ca khaṇḍaḥ kāpālikas tathā // HYP_1.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhānukī</s>, <s>Nāradeva</s>, <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Kāpālika</s> — // HYP 1.8 //

children.text: ity ādayo mahāsiddhā haṭha-yoga-prabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: These and other <s>Mahāsiddhas</s> (great perfected ones), through the power of <s>Haṭha Yoga</s>,

children.text: khaṇḍayitvā kāla-daṇḍaṃ brahmāṇḍe vicaranti te // HYP_1.9 //
children.translated_text: Having broken the staff of <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death), wander freely throughout the universe. // HYP 1.9 //

children.text: aśeṣa-tāpa-taptānāṃ samāśraya-maṭho haṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those scorched by all [manner of] afflictions, <s>Haṭha</s> [Yoga] is the sheltering monastery;

children.text: aśeṣa-yoga-yuktānām ādhāra-kamaṭho haṭhaḥ // HYP_1.10 //
children.translated_text: For those engaged in all [types of] <s>yoga</s>, <s>Haṭha</s> is the supporting tortoise. // HYP 1.10 //

children.text: haṭha-vidyā paraṃ gopyā yoginā siddhim icchatā /
children.translated_text: The science of <s>Haṭha</s> should be kept supremely secret by the <s>yogī</s> who desires <s>siddhi</s> (perfection);

children.text: bhaved vīryavatī guptā nirvīryā tu prakāśitā // HYP_1.11 //
children.translated_text: It becomes powerful when kept secret, and powerless when revealed. // HYP 1.11 //

children.text: surājye dhārmike deśe subhikṣe nirupadrave /
children.translated_text: In a well-governed, righteous land, with abundant food and free from disturbance,

children.text: dhanuḥ pramāṇa-paryantaṃ śilāgni-jala-varjite /
children.translated_text: Within a space of a bow's length, free from stones, fire, and water,

children.text: ekānte maṭhikā-madhye sthātavyaṃ haṭha-yoginā // HYP_1.12 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Haṭha yogī</s> should dwell in solitude within a small hermitage. // HYP 1.12 //

children.text: alpa-dvāram arandhra-garta-vivaraṃ nātyucca-nīcāyataṃ
children.translated_text: With a small door, without holes, hollows, or crevices, neither too high nor too low nor too long,

children.text: samyag-gomaya-sāndra-liptam amalaṃ niḥśesa-jantūjjhitam /
children.translated_text: Well-smeared with fresh cow-dung, clean, free from all insects,

children.text: bāhye maṇḍapa-vedi-kūpa-ruciraṃ prākāra-saṃveṣṭitaṃ
children.translated_text: With a pleasant pavilion, platform, and well outside, enclosed by a wall —

children.text: proktaṃ yoga-maṭhasya lakṣaṇam idaṃ siddhair haṭhābhyāsibhiḥ // HYP_1.13 //
children.translated_text: This is the description of a <s>yoga maṭha</s> (hermitage), as stated by the <s>Siddhas</s> who practice <s>Haṭha</s>. // HYP 1.13 //

children.text: evaṃ vidhe maṭhe sthitvā sarva-cintā-vivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dwelling in such a hermitage, free from all anxieties,

children.text: gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa yogam eva samabhyaset // HYP_1.14 //
children.translated_text: One should practice <s>yoga</s> alone, following the path instructed by the <s>Guru</s>. // HYP 1.14 //

children.text: atyāhāraḥ prayāsaś ca prajalpo niyamāgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Overeating, overexertion, excessive talking, rigid adherence to rules,

children.text: jana-saṅgaś ca laulyaṃ ca ṣaḍbhir yogo vinaśyati // HYP_1.15 //
children.translated_text: Company of people, and fickleness — by these six, <s>yoga</s> is destroyed. // HYP 1.15 //

children.text: utsāhāt sāhasād dhairyāt tattva-jñānāś ca niścayāt /
children.translated_text: By enthusiasm, courage, perseverance, knowledge of truth, firm resolve,

children.text: jana-saṅga-parityāgāt ṣaḍbhir yogaḥ prasiddhyati // HYP_1.16 //
children.translated_text: And abandonment of the company of people — by these six, <s>yoga</s> succeeds. // HYP 1.16 //

children.text: ahiṃsā satyam asteyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing), <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), <s>kṣamā</s> (forgiveness), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness),

children.text: dayārjavaṃ mitāhāraḥ śaucaṃ caiva yamā daśa // HYP_1.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dayā</s> (compassion), <s>ārjava</s> (sincerity), <s>mitāhāra</s> (moderate diet), and <s>śauca</s> (purity) — these are the ten <s>Yamas</s>. // HYP 1.17 //

children.text: tapaḥ santoṣa āstikyaṃ dānam īśvara-pūjanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tapas</s> (austerity), <s>santoṣa</s> (contentment), <s>āstikya</s> (faith), <s>dāna</s> (charity), <s>īśvara-pūjana</s> (worship of the Lord),

children.text: siddhānta-vākya-śravaṇaṃ hrīmatī ca tapo hutam /
children.translated_text: Hearing of scriptural teachings, <s>hrī</s> (modesty), <s>mati</s> (intellect), <s>tapa</s> (austerity), and <s>huta</s> (oblation) —

children.text: niyamā daśa samproktā yoga-śāstra-viśāradaiḥ // HYP_1.18 //
children.translated_text: These ten <s>Niyamas</s> are declared by those learned in the <s>yoga śāstras</s>. // HYP 1.18 //

children.text: haṭhasya prathamāṅgatvād āsanaṃ pūrvam ucyate /
children.translated_text: Since <s>āsana</s> is the first limb of <s>Haṭha</s> [Yoga], it is described first;

children.text: kuryāt tad āsanaṃ sthairyam ārogyaṃ cāṅga-lāghavam // HYP_1.19 //
children.translated_text: One should practice that <s>āsana</s> which gives steadiness, health, and lightness of limbs. // HYP 1.19 //

children.text: vaśiṣṭhādyaiś ca munibhir matsyendrādyaiś ca yogibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By sages such as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others, and by <s>yogīs</s> such as <s>Matsyendra</s> and others,

children.text: aṅgīkṛtāny āsanāni kathyante kānicin mayā // HYP_1.20 //
children.translated_text: The <s>āsanas</s> that have been accepted — some of them are described by me. // HYP 1.20 //

children.text: jānūrvor antare samyak kṛtvā pāda-tale ubhe /
children.translated_text: Having placed both soles of the feet properly between the knees and thighs,

children.text: ṛju-kāyaḥ samāsīnaḥ svastikaṃ tat pracakṣate // HYP_1.21 //
children.translated_text: Sitting upright with a straight body — this is called <s>Svastikāsana</s>. // HYP 1.21 //

children.text: savye dakṣiṇa-gulphaṃ tu pṛṣṭha-pārśve niyojayet /
children.translated_text: One should place the left ankle on the back side of the right [thigh],

children.text: dakṣiṇe'pi tathā savyaṃ gomukhaṃ gomukhākṛtiḥ // HYP_1.22 //
children.translated_text: And similarly the right [ankle] on the left — this is <s>Gomukhāsana</s>, resembling a cow's face. // HYP 1.22 //

children.text: ekaṃ pādaṃ tathaikasmin vinyased uruṇi sthiram /
children.translated_text: Placing one foot firmly on the other thigh,

children.text: itarasmiṃs tathā coruṃ vīrāsanam itīritam // HYP_1.23 //
children.translated_text: And the other [foot] similarly on the other thigh — this is called <s>Vīrāsana</s> (hero's posture). // HYP 1.23 //

children.text: gudaṃ nirudhya gulphābhyāṃ vyutkrameṇa samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pressing the anus firmly with the crossed ankles, with concentration,

children.text: kūrmāsanaṃ bhaved etad iti yoga-vido viduḥ // HYP_1.24 //
children.translated_text: This becomes <s>Kūrmāsana</s> (tortoise posture) — thus the knowers of <s>yoga</s> know. // HYP 1.24 //

children.text: padmāsanaṃ tu saṃsthāpya jānūrvor antare karau /
children.translated_text: Establishing <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), placing the hands between the knees and thighs,

children.text: niveśya bhūmau saṃsthāpya vyomasthaṃ kukkuṭāsanam // HYP_1.25 //
children.translated_text: And planting them on the ground, rising up in the air — this is <s>Kukkuṭāsana</s> (cock posture). // HYP 1.25 //

children.text: kukkuṭāsana-bandha-stho dorbhyāṃ sambadya kandharām /
children.translated_text: Being bound in <s>Kukkuṭāsana</s>, clasping the neck with both arms,

children.text: bhaved kūrmavad uttāna etad uttāna-kūrmakam // HYP_1.26 //
children.translated_text: Lying on the back like a tortoise — this is <s>Uttāna Kūrmaka</s> (supine tortoise). // HYP 1.26 //

children.text: pādāṅguṣṭhau tu pāṇibhyāṃ gṛhītvā śravaṇāvadhi /
children.translated_text: Grasping the toes of both feet with the hands, pulling them up to the ears,

children.text: dhanur ākarṣaṇaṃ kuryād dhanur-āsanam ucyate // HYP_1.27 //
children.translated_text: One should draw [them] like a bow — this is called <s>Dhanurāsana</s> (bow posture). // HYP 1.27 //

children.text: vāmoru-mūlārpita-dakṣa-pādaṃ
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot at the base of the left thigh,

children.text: jānor bahir veṣṭita-vāma-pādam /
children.translated_text: The left foot wrapped outside the right knee,

children.text: pragṛhya tiṣṭhet parivartitāṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: Holding [the foot], one should sit with the body turned —

children.text: śrī-matysanāthoditam āsanaṃ syāt // HYP_1.28 //
children.translated_text: This is the <s>āsana</s> taught by the revered <s>Matsyanātha</s>. // HYP 1.28 //

children.text: matsyendra-pīṭhaṃ jaṭhara-pradīptiṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Matsyendrapīṭha</s> (the seat of Matsyendra) kindles the digestive fire,

children.text: pracaṇḍa-rug maṇḍala-khaṇḍanāstram /
children.translated_text: It is a weapon that shatters the circle of fierce diseases;

children.text: abhyāsataḥ kuṇḍalinī-prabodhaṃ
children.translated_text: Through practice, it grants the awakening of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>

children.text: candra-sthiratvaṃ ca dadāti puṃsām // HYP_1.29 //
children.translated_text: And stability of the moon-[<s>bindu</s>] for men. // HYP 1.29 //

children.text: prasārya pādau bhuvi daṇḍa-rūpau
children.translated_text: Stretching the legs on the ground like sticks,

children.text: dorbhyāṃ padāgra-dvitayaṃ gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: Grasping the tips of both feet with the hands,

children.text: jānūparinyasta-lalāṭa-deśo
children.translated_text: Placing the forehead upon the knees —

children.text: vased idaṃ paścimatānam āhuḥ // HYP_1.30 //
children.translated_text: One should abide [thus]; this they call <s>Paścimatāna</s> (the back-stretch). // HYP 1.30 //

children.text: iti paścimatānam āsanāgryaṃ
children.translated_text: This <s>Paścimatāna</s>, the foremost of <s>āsanas</s>,

children.text: pavanaṃ paścima-vāhinaṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: Makes the breath flow along the back;

children.text: udayaṃ jaṭharānalasya kuryād
children.translated_text: It kindles the gastric fire

children.text: udare kārśyam arogatāṃ ca puṃsām // HYP_1.31 //
children.translated_text: And produces slimness and freedom from disease in men. // HYP 1.31 //

children.text: dharām avaṣṭabhya kara-dvayena
children.translated_text: Supporting the earth with both palms,

children.text: tat-kūrpara-sthāpita-nābhi-pārśvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sides of the navel resting on the elbows,

children.text: uccāsano daṇḍavad utthitaḥ khe
children.translated_text: Raised high, the body rigid like a stick in the air —

children.text: māyūram etat pravadanti pīṭham // HYP_1.32 //
children.translated_text: This they call <s>Māyūra Pīṭha</s> (the peacock posture). // HYP 1.32 //

children.text: harati sakala-rogān āśu gulmodarādīn
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrī Mayūrāsana</s> quickly removes all diseases such as abdominal tumors,

children.text: abhibhavati ca doṣān āsanaṃ śrī-mayūram /
children.translated_text: And overcomes [the imbalance of] the <s>doṣas</s>;

children.text: bahu kadaśana-bhuktaṃ bhasma kuryād aśeṣaṃ
children.translated_text: It completely digests even unwholesome food,

children.text: janayati jaṭharāgniṃ jārayet kāla-kūṭam // HYP_1.33 //
children.translated_text: Kindles the gastric fire, and can digest even the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison). // HYP 1.33 //

children.text: uttānaṃ śabavad bhūmau śayanaṃ tac chavāsanam /
children.translated_text: Lying flat on the ground face-up like a corpse — that is <s>Śavāsana</s> (corpse posture);

children.text: śavāsanaṃ śrānti-haraṃ citta-viśrānti-kārakam // HYP_1.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śavāsana</s> removes fatigue and brings rest to the mind. // HYP 1.34 //

children.text: caturaśīty āsanāni śivena kathitāni ca /
children.translated_text: Eighty-four <s>āsanas</s> were taught by <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: tebhyaś catuṣkam ādāya sārabhūtaṃ bravīmy aham // HYP_1.35 //
children.translated_text: Taking four from among them, the essential ones, I describe. // HYP 1.35 //

children.text: siddhaṃ padmaṃ tathā siṃhaṃ bhadraṃ veti catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Siddha</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Siṃha</s>, and <s>Bhadra</s> — these are the four;

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ tatrāpi ca sukhe tiṣṭhet siddhāsane sadā // HYP_1.36 //
children.translated_text: Among these, the best is to always sit comfortably in <s>Siddhāsana</s>. // HYP 1.36 //

children.text: yoni-sthānakam aṅghri-mūla-ghaṭitaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhaṃ vinyaset
children.translated_text: Having firmly placed one heel at the perineum (<s>yoni-sthāna</s>),

children.text: meṇḍhre pādam athaikam eva hṛdaye kṛtvā hanuṃ susthiram /
children.translated_text: The other foot placed above the generative organ, with the chin firmly at the heart,

children.text: sthāṇuḥ saṃyamitendriyo'cala-dṛśā paśyed bhruvor antaraṃ
children.translated_text: Steady as a pillar, with senses restrained, gazing with unwavering eyes at the space between the eyebrows —

children.text: hy etan mokṣa-kapāṭa-bheda-janakaṃ siddhāsanaṃ procyate // HYP_1.37 //
children.translated_text: This, which opens the door to liberation, is called <s>Siddhāsana</s>. // HYP 1.37 //

children.text: meṇḍhrād upari vinyasya savyaṃ gulphaṃ tathopari /
children.translated_text: Placing the left ankle above the generative organ, and the other above that,

children.text: gulphāntaraṃ ca nikṣipya siddhāsanam idaṃ bhavet // HYP_1.38 //
children.translated_text: And placing the [second] ankle [there] — this becomes <s>Siddhāsana</s>. // HYP 1.38 //

children.text: etat siddhāsanaṃ prāhur anye vajrāsanaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: This is called <s>Siddhāsana</s> by some; others know it as <s>Vajrāsana</s>;

children.text: muktāsanaṃ vadanty eke prāhur guptāsanaṃ pare // HYP_1.39 //
children.translated_text: Some call it <s>Muktāsana</s>, and others call it <s>Guptāsana</s>. // HYP 1.39 //

children.text: yameṣv iva mitāhāram ahiṃsā niyameṣv iva /
children.translated_text: Just as moderate diet is the chief among the <s>Yamas</s>, and non-violence among the <s>Niyamas</s>,

children.text: mukhyaṃ sarvāsaneṣv ekaṃ siddhāḥ siddhāsanaṃ viduḥ // HYP_1.40 //
children.translated_text: So the <s>Siddhas</s> know <s>Siddhāsana</s> to be the foremost among all <s>āsanas</s>. // HYP 1.40 //

children.text: caturaśīti-pīṭheṣu siddham eva sadābhyaset /
children.translated_text: Among the eighty-four <s>āsanas</s>, one should always practice <s>Siddhāsana</s>;

children.text: dvāsaptati-sahasrāṇāṃ nāḍīnāṃ mala-śodhanam // HYP_1.41 //
children.translated_text: It purifies the impurities of the seventy-two thousand <s>nāḍīs</s> (energy channels). // HYP 1.41 //

children.text: ātma-dhyāyī mitāhārī yāvad dvādaśa-vatsaram /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> who meditates on the self and eats moderately, for twelve years,

children.text: sadā siddhāsanābhyāsād yogī niṣpattim āpnuyāt // HYP_1.42 //
children.translated_text: Through the constant practice of <s>Siddhāsana</s>, attains perfection (<s>niṣpatti</s>). // HYP 1.42 //

children.text: kim anyair bahubhiḥ pīṭhaiḥ siddhe siddhāsane sati /
children.translated_text: What need is there of many other <s>āsanas</s> when <s>Siddhāsana</s> is accomplished?

children.text: prāṇānile sāvadhāne baddhe kevala-kumbhake /
children.translated_text: When the <s>prāṇa</s> breath is carefully [controlled] and <s>Kevala Kumbhaka</s> (spontaneous retention) is achieved,

children.text: utpadyate nirāyāsāt svayam evonmanī kalā // HYP_1.43 //
children.translated_text: The state of <s>Unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind) arises effortlessly of its own accord. // HYP 1.43 //

children.text: tathaikāsminn eva dṛḍhe siddhe siddhāsane sati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, when the one firm <s>Siddhāsana</s> is accomplished,

children.text: bandha-trayam anāyāsāt svayam evopajāyate // HYP_1.44 //
children.translated_text: The three <s>Bandhas</s> (locks) arise effortlessly of their own accord. // HYP 1.44 //

children.text: nāsanaṃ siddha-sadṛśaṃ na kumbhaḥ kevalopamaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>āsana</s> equal to <s>Siddha</s>, no <s>kumbhaka</s> comparable to <s>Kevala</s>,

children.text: na khecarī-samā mudrā na nāda-sadṛśo layaḥ // HYP_1.45 //
children.translated_text: No <s>mudrā</s> equal to <s>Khecarī</s>, and no <s>laya</s> (dissolution) equal to <s>Nāda</s> (inner sound). // HYP 1.45 //

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ ca caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot on the left thigh, and similarly the left

children.text: dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: On the right thigh, grasping [the toes] firmly from behind with both hands,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayet
children.translated_text: Placing the chin on the chest, gazing at the tip of the nose —

children.text: etad vyādhi-vināśa-kāri yamināṃ padmāsanaṃ procyate // HYP_1.46 //
children.translated_text: This, which destroys diseases, is called <s>Padmāsana</s> for those with self-control. // HYP 1.46 //

children.text: uttānau caraṇau kṛtvā ūru-saṃsthau prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Placing both feet, soles upward, carefully on the thighs,

children.text: ūru-madhye tathottānau pāṇī kṛtvā tato dṛśau // HYP_1.47 //
children.translated_text: And both palms likewise upturned in the middle of the thighs, then the gaze — // HYP 1.47 //

children.text: nāsāgre vinyased rājad-anta-mūle tu jihvayā /
children.translated_text: One should fix [the gaze] at the tip of the nose, the tongue pressed against the base of the upper teeth,

children.text: uttambhya cibukaṃ vakṣasy utthāpy pavanaṃ śanaiḥ // HYP_1.48 //
children.translated_text: The chin raised to the chest, slowly raising the breath. // HYP 1.48 //

children.text: idaṃ padmāsanaṃ proktaṃ sarva-vyādhi-vināśanam /
children.translated_text: This is declared to be <s>Padmāsana</s>, the destroyer of all diseases;

children.text: durlabhaṃ yena kenāpi dhīmatā labhyate bhuvi // HYP_1.49 //
children.translated_text: Difficult to attain by just anyone, it is achieved on earth only by the wise. // HYP 1.49 //

children.text: kṛtvā sampuṭitau karau dṛḍhataraṃ baddhvā tu padmāsanaṃ
children.translated_text: Having cupped the hands firmly together and bound in <s>Padmāsana</s>,

children.text: gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi sannidhāya cibukaṃ dhyāyaṃś ca tac cetasi /
children.translated_text: Pressing the chin firmly against the chest, meditating on that [Brahman] in the mind,

children.text: vāraṃ vāram apānam ūrdhvam anilaṃ protsārayan pūritaṃ
children.translated_text: Repeatedly driving the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) upward, and releasing the filled <s>prāṇa</s> downward —

children.text: nyañcan prāṇam upaiti bodham atulaṃ śakti-prabhāvān naraḥ // HYP_1.50 //
children.translated_text: A person attains incomparable awakening through the power of <s>Śakti</s>. // HYP 1.50 //

children.text: padmāsane sthito yogī nāḍī-dvāreṇa pūritam /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> seated in <s>Padmāsana</s>, who retains the breath

children.text: mārutaṃ dhārayed yas tu sa mukto nātra saṃśayaḥ // HYP_1.51 //
children.translated_text: Drawn in through the <s>nāḍī</s> openings — he is liberated, there is no doubt. // HYP 1.51 //

children.text: atha siṃhāsanam-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Siṃhāsana</s> (lion posture):

children.text: gulphau ca vṛṣaṇasyādhaḥ sīvanyāḥ pārśvayoḥ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: One should place both ankles below the scrotum, on either side of the perineum,

children.text: dakṣiṇe savya-gulphaṃ tu dakṣa-gulphaṃ tu savyake // HYP_1.52 //
children.translated_text: The left ankle on the right [side] and the right ankle on the left. // HYP 1.52 //

children.text: hastau tu jānvoḥ saṃsthāpya svāṅgulīḥ samprasārya ca /
children.translated_text: Placing the hands on the knees and spreading the fingers,

children.text: vyātta-vaktro nirīkṣeta nāsāgraṃ susamāhitaḥ // HYP_1.53 //
children.translated_text: With mouth wide open, one should gaze at the tip of the nose with full concentration. // HYP 1.53 //

children.text: siṃhāsanaṃ bhaved etat pūjitaṃ yogi-puṅgavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This becomes <s>Siṃhāsana</s>, venerated by the best of <s>yogīs</s>;

children.text: bandha-tritaya-sandhānaṃ kurute cāsanottamam // HYP_1.54 //
children.translated_text: This excellent <s>āsana</s> facilitates the union of the three <s>Bandhas</s> (locks). // HYP 1.54 //

children.text: atha bhadrāsanam-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Bhadrāsana</s> (auspicious posture):

children.text: gulphau ca vṛṣaṇasyādhaḥ sīvanyāḥ pārśvayoḥ kṣipte /
children.translated_text: Both ankles are placed below the scrotum, on either side of the perineum,

children.text: savya-gulphaṃ tathā savye dakṣa-gulphaṃ tu dakṣiṇe // HYP_1.55 //
children.translated_text: The left ankle on the left side and the right ankle on the right. // HYP 1.55 //

children.text: pārśva-pādau ca pāṇibhyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā suniścalam /
children.translated_text: Holding the feet at the sides firmly with both hands, completely still,

children.text: bhadrāsanaṃ bhaved etat sarva-vyādhi-vināśanam /
children.translated_text: This becomes <s>Bhadrāsana</s>, the destroyer of all diseases;

children.text: gorakṣāsanam ity āhur idaṃ vai siddha-yoginaḥ // HYP_1.56 //
children.translated_text: The accomplished <s>yogīs</s> call this <s>Gorakṣāsana</s>. // HYP 1.56 //

children.text: evam āsana-bandheṣu yogīndro vigata-śramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the king of <s>yogīs</s>, having mastered the posture-locks and being free from fatigue,

children.text: abhyasen nāḍikā-śuddhiṃ mudrādi-pavanī-kriyām // HYP_1.57 //
children.translated_text: Should practice purification of the <s>nāḍīs</s>, <s>mudrās</s>, and breath-control techniques. // HYP 1.57 //

children.text: āsanaṃ kumbhakaṃ citraṃ mudrākhyaṃ karaṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Āsana</s> (posture), <s>Kumbhaka</s> (breath retention), the various <s>Mudrās</s> (seals), and then

children.text: atha nādānusandhānam abhyāsānukramo haṭhe // HYP_1.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nāda-anusandhāna</s> (meditation on inner sound) — this is the order of practice in <s>Haṭha</s> [Yoga]. // HYP 1.58 //

children.text: brahmacārī mitāhārī tyāgī yoga-parāyaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is celibate, eats moderately, is renounced, and devoted to <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: abdād ūrdhvaṃ bhavet siddho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // HYP_1.59 //
children.translated_text: After a year becomes a <s>Siddha</s> (perfected one) — there need be no deliberation on this. // HYP 1.59 //

children.text: susnigdha-madhurāhāraś caturthāṃśa-vivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Food that is very unctuous and sweet, leaving one-fourth [of the stomach] empty,

children.text: bhujyate śiva-samprītyai mitāhāraḥ sa ucyate // HYP_1.60 //
children.translated_text: Eaten for the pleasure of <s>Śiva</s> — that is called <s>mitāhāra</s> (moderate diet). // HYP 1.60 //

children.text: kaṭvāmla-tīkṣṇa-lavaṇoṣṇa-harīta-śāka-
children.translated_text: Bitter, sour, pungent, salty, hot foods, green vegetables,

children.text: sauvīra-taila-tila-sarṣapa-madya-matsyān /
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvīra</s> (sour gruel), sesame oil, sesame seeds, mustard, alcohol, fish,

children.text: ājādi-māṃsa-dadhi-takra-kulatthakola-
children.translated_text: Goat and other meats, curds, buttermilk, <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram), <s>kola</s> (jujube),

children.text: piṇyāka-hiṅgu-laśunādyam apathyam āhuḥ // HYP_1.61 //
children.translated_text: Oil-cake, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), garlic, and the like — these are said to be unwholesome. // HYP 1.61 //

children.text: bhojanam ahitaṃ vidyāt punar asyoṣṇī-kṛtaṃ rūkṣam /
children.translated_text: One should know as harmful: food that is reheated, that is dry,

children.text: atilavaṇam amla-yuktaṃ kadaśana-śākotkaṃ varjyam // HYP_1.62 //
children.translated_text: That is excessively salty, mixed with sour [substances], and that consists of excessive vegetables — these should be avoided. // HYP 1.62 //

body.translated_text: In the beginning, one should avoid [the use of] fire, women, and travel. // HYP 1.63 //

children.text: tathā hi gorakṣa-vacanam-
children.translated_text: As <s>Gorakṣa</s> has said:

children.text: varjayed durjana-prāntaṃ vahni-strī-pathi-sevanam /
children.translated_text: One should avoid the company of wicked people, [excessive use of] fire, women, and travel,

children.text: prātaḥ-snānopavāsādi kāya-kleśa-vidhiṃ tathā // HYP_1.64 //
children.translated_text: Morning baths, fasting, and other practices that cause physical distress. // HYP 1.64 //

children.text: godhūma-śāli-yava-ṣāṣṭika-śobhanānnaṃ
children.translated_text: Wheat, rice, barley, <s>ṣāṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice), excellent food,

children.text: kṣīrājya-khaṇḍa-navanīta-siddhā-madhūni /
children.translated_text: Milk, ghee, sugar, fresh butter, and honey,

children.text: śuṇṭhī-paṭola-kaphalādika-pañca-śākaṃ
children.translated_text: Dried ginger, <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), the five vegetables beginning with <s>kaphalā</s>,

children.text: mudgādi-divyam udakaṃ ca yamīndra-pathyam // HYP_1.65 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mudga</s> (mung beans) and other [pulses], pure water — these are beneficial for the master of <s>Yamas</s>. // HYP 1.65 //

children.text: puṣṭaṃ sumadhuraṃ snigdhaṃ gavyaṃ dhātu-prapoṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> should eat food that is nourishing, very sweet, unctuous, made of cow's milk, strengthening to the bodily tissues,

children.text: manobhilaṣitaṃ yogyaṃ yogī bhojanam ācaret // HYP_1.66 //
children.translated_text: Pleasing to the mind, and suitable [for yoga practice]. // HYP 1.66 //

children.text: yuvo vṛddho'tivṛddho vā vyādhito durbalo'pi vā /
children.translated_text: Whether young, old, very old, sick, or weak,

children.text: abhyāsāt siddhim āpnoti sarva-yogeṣv atandritaḥ // HYP_1.67 //
children.translated_text: Through practice, one attains <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) in all forms of <s>yoga</s>, if one is diligent. // HYP 1.67 //

children.text: kriyā-yuktasya siddhiḥ syād akriyasya kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Success comes to the one who is engaged in practice; how can it come to the inactive?

children.text: na śāstra-pāṭha-mātreṇa yoga-siddhiḥ prajāyate // HYP_1.68 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga siddhi</s> (yogic perfection) is not born from mere reading of scriptures. // HYP 1.68 //

children.text: na veṣa-dhāraṇaṃ siddheḥ kāraṇaṃ na ca tat-kathā /
children.translated_text: Wearing [special] garments is not the cause of <s>siddhi</s>, nor is talking about it;

children.text: kriyaiva kāraṇaṃ siddheḥ satyam etan na saṃśayaḥ // HYP_1.69 //
children.translated_text: Practice alone is the cause of <s>siddhi</s> — this is the truth, without doubt. // HYP 1.69 //

children.text: pīṭhāni kumbhakāś citrā divyāni karaṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>āsanas</s>, the various <s>kumbhakas</s>, and the divine <s>karaṇas</s> (techniques/mudrās) —

children.text: sarvāṇy api haṭhābhyāse rāja-yoga-phalāvadhi // HYP_1.70 //
children.translated_text: All [practices] of <s>Haṭha</s> are meant to culminate in the fruit of <s>Rāja Yoga</s>. // HYP 1.70 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the First Instruction in the <s>Haṭha Pradīpikā</s>.

children.text: athāsane dṛdhe yogī vaśī hita-mitāśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, when the <s>yogī</s> is firm in <s>āsana</s>, self-controlled, eating wholesome and moderate food,

children.text: gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa prāṇāyāmān samabhyaset // HYP_2.1 //
children.translated_text: He should practice <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) following the path instructed by the <s>Guru</s>. // HYP 2.1 //

body.text: cale vāte calaṃ cittaṃ niścale niścalaṃ bhavet // HYP_2.
body.translated_text: When the breath (<s>vāta</s>) is unsteady, the mind is unsteady; when [the breath] is steady, [the mind] becomes steady. // HYP 2.

body.text: yogī sthāṇutvam āpnoti tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet // HYP_2.2 //
body.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> attains steadiness — therefore one should restrain the breath. // HYP 2.2 //

children.text: yāvad vāyuḥ sthito dehe tāvaj jīvanam ucyate /
children.translated_text: As long as the breath remains in the body, that is called life;

children.text: maraṇaṃ tasya niṣkrāntis tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet // HYP_2.3 //
children.translated_text: death is its departure — therefore one should restrain the breath. (HYP 2.3)

children.text: malākalāsu nāḍīṣu māruto naiva madhyagaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) are full of impurities, the breath does not enter the middle [channel],

children.text: kathaṃ syād unmanībhāvaḥ kārya-siddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // HYP_2.4 //
children.translated_text: how then can the state of <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind) arise? How can the goal be accomplished? (HYP 2.4)

children.text: śuddham eti yadā sarvaṃ nāḍī-cakraṃ malākulam /
children.translated_text: When the entire network of <s>nāḍīs</s>, filled with impurities, becomes purified,

children.text: tadaiva jāyate yogī prāṇa-saṃgrahaṇe kṣamaḥ // HYP_2.5 //
children.translated_text: only then does the <s>yogī</s> become capable of controlling <s>prāṇa</s>. (HYP 2.5)

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ tataḥ kuryān nityaṃ sāttvikayā dhiyā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) regularly with a <s>sāttvic</s> (pure) disposition,

children.text: yathā suṣumṇā-nāḍīsthā malāḥ śuddhiṃ prayānti ca // HYP_2.6 //
children.translated_text: so that the impurities in the <s>suṣumnā nāḍī</s> may be purified. (HYP 2.6)

children.text: baddha-padmāsano yogī prāṇaṃ candreṇa pūrayet /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s>, seated in <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), should inhale <s>prāṇa</s> through the lunar [channel] (<s>iḍā</s>),

children.text: dhārayitvā yathā-śakti bhūyaḥ sūryeṇa recayet // HYP_2.7 //
children.translated_text: retain it as long as possible, and then exhale through the solar [channel] (<s>piṅgalā</s>). (HYP 2.7)

children.text: prāṇaṃ sūryeṇa cākṛṣya pūrayed udaraṃ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Drawing <s>prāṇa</s> through the solar [channel], one should slowly fill the abdomen,

children.text: vidhivat kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā punaś candreṇa recayet // HYP_2.8 //
children.translated_text: having performed <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention) according to the prescribed method, one should exhale again through the lunar [channel]. (HYP 2.8)

children.text: yena tyajet tena pītvā dhārayed atirodhataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having inhaled through the [channel] through which one exhales, one should retain [the breath] without excessive force,

children.text: recayec ca tato'nyena śanair eva na vegataḥ // HYP_2.9 //
children.translated_text: and then exhale through the other [channel], slowly and not forcefully. (HYP 2.9)

children.text: prāṇaṃ ced iḍayā piben niyamitaṃ bhūyo'nyathā recayet
children.translated_text: If one inhales <s>prāṇa</s> through <s>iḍā</s> in a regulated manner, one should exhale through the other,

children.text: pītvā piṅgalayā samīraṇam atho baddhvā tyajed vāmayā /
children.translated_text: having inhaled through <s>piṅgalā</s>, and then having retained, one should release through the left,

children.text: sūrya-candramasor anena vidhinābhyāsaṃ sadā tanvatāṃ
children.translated_text: by this method of practice through the sun and moon [channels], always extending the practice,

children.text: śuddhā nāḍi-gaṇā bhavanti yamināṃ māsa-trayād ūrdhvataḥ // HYP_2.10 //
children.translated_text: the group of <s>nāḍīs</s> of the practitioners becomes purified after three months. (HYP 2.10)

children.text: prātar madhyandine sāyam ardha-rātre ca kumbhakān /
children.translated_text: In the morning, at midday, in the evening, and at midnight, one should practice <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention),

children.text: śanair aśīti-paryantaṃ catur vāraṃ samabhyaset // HYP_2.11 //
children.translated_text: gradually up to eighty [retentions], four times [a day]. (HYP 2.11)

children.text: kanīyasi bhaved sveda kampo bhavati madhyame /
children.translated_text: In the lowest [stage] there is perspiration, in the middle stage trembling,

children.text: uttame sthānam āpnoti tato vāyuṃ nibandhayet // HYP_2.12 //
children.translated_text: in the highest [stage] one attains steadiness — therefore one should restrain the breath. (HYP 2.12)

children.text: jalena śrama-jātena gātra-mardanam ācaret /
children.translated_text: One should rub the body with the sweat produced by exertion,

children.text: dṛḍhatā laghutā caiva tena gātrasya jāyate // HYP_2.13 //
children.translated_text: by this, firmness and lightness of the body arise. (HYP 2.13)

children.text: abhyāsa-kāle prathame śastaṃ kṣīrājya-bhojanam /
children.translated_text: In the initial period of practice, food with milk and ghee is recommended,

children.text: tato'bhyāse dṛḍhībhūte na tādṛṅ-niyama-grahaḥ // HYP_2.14 //
children.translated_text: when the practice becomes firm, such strict rules need not be observed. (HYP 2.14)

children.text: yathā siṃho gajo vyāghro bhaved vaśyaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a lion, elephant, or tiger is tamed slowly and gradually,

children.text: tathaiva sevito vāyur anyathā hanti sādhakam // HYP_2.15 //
children.translated_text: so too the breath should be controlled; otherwise it kills the practitioner. (HYP 2.15)

children.text: prāṇāyāmena yuktena sarva-roga-kṣayo bhavet /
children.translated_text: By proper <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, all diseases are destroyed,

children.text: ayuktābhyāsa-yogena sarva-roga-samudgamaḥ // HYP_2.16 //
children.translated_text: by improper practice, all diseases arise. (HYP 2.16)

children.text: hikkā śvāsaś ca kāsaś ca śiraḥ-karṇākṣi-vedanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hiccups, asthma, cough, and pains in the head, ears, and eyes —

children.text: bhavanti vividhāḥ rogāḥ pavanasya prakopataḥ // HYP_2.17 //
children.translated_text: various diseases arise from the disturbance of the breath. (HYP 2.17)

children.text: yuktaṃ yuktaṃ tyajed vāyuṃ yuktaṃ yuktaṃ ca pūrayet /
children.translated_text: One should release the breath in due measure, fill it in due measure,

children.text: yuktaṃ yuktaṃ ca badhnīyād evaṃ siddhim avāpnuyāt // HYP_2.18 //
children.translated_text: and retain it in due measure — thus one attains accomplishment. (HYP 2.18)

children.text: yadā tu nāḍī-śuddhiḥ syāt tathā cihnāni bāhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: When the purification of the <s>nāḍīs</s> occurs, then external signs appear —

children.text: kāyasya kṛśatā kāntis tadā jāyate niścitam // HYP_2.19 //
children.translated_text: leanness and radiance of the body certainly arise. (HYP 2.19)

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ dhāraṇaṃ vāyor analasya pradīpanam /
children.translated_text: The ability to retain breath at will, the kindling of the digestive fire,

children.text: nādābhivyaktir ārogyaṃ jāyate nāḍi-śodhanāt // HYP_2.20 //
children.translated_text: the manifestation of the inner sound (<s>nāda</s>), and health arise from the purification of the <s>nāḍīs</s>. (HYP 2.20)

children.text: meda-śleṣmādhikaḥ pūrvaṃ ṣaṭ-karmāṇi samācaret /
children.translated_text: One who has excess fat and phlegm should first perform the six cleansing actions (<s>ṣaṭkarma</s>),

children.text: anyas tu nācaret tāni doṣāṇāṃ samabhāvataḥ // HYP_2.21 //
children.translated_text: but others need not perform them, due to the balance of the <s>doṣas</s>. (HYP 2.21)

children.text: dhautir bastis tathā netis trāṭakaṃ naulikaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhauti</s>, <s>Basti</s>, <s>Neti</s>, <s>Trāṭaka</s>, <s>Nauli</s>,

children.text: kapāla-bhātiś caitāni ṣaṭ-karmāṇi pracakṣate // HYP_2.22 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Kapālabhāti</s> — these are declared to be the six cleansing actions. (HYP 2.22)

children.text: karma ṣaṭkam idaṃ gopyaṃ ghaṭa-śodhana-kārakam /
children.translated_text: These six actions are to be kept secret and are effective in purifying the body,

children.text: vicitra-guṇa-sandhāya pūjyate yogi-puṅgavaiḥ // HYP_2.23 //
children.translated_text: they are endowed with wondrous qualities and are honored by the foremost <s>yogīs</s>. (HYP 2.23)

children.text: tatra dhautiḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Dhauti</s>:

children.text: catur-aṅgula-vistāraṃ hasta-pañca-daśāyatam /
children.translated_text: A cloth four finger-breadths wide and fifteen hand-spans long,

children.text: gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa siktaṃ vastraṃ śanair graset /
children.translated_text: moistened, should be slowly swallowed following the method taught by the <s>guru</s>,

children.text: punaḥ pratyāharec caitad uditaṃ dhauti-karma tat // HYP_2.24 //
children.translated_text: and then drawn out again — this is the practice of <s>Dhauti</s>. (HYP 2.24)

children.text: kāsa-śvāsa-plīha-kuṣṭhaṃ kapharogāś ca viṃśatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Cough, asthma, diseases of the spleen, leprosy, and twenty diseases caused by <s>kapha</s> —

children.text: dhauti-karma-prabhāveṇa prayānty eva na saṃśayaḥ // HYP_2.25 //
children.translated_text: all these are certainly destroyed by the power of <s>Dhauti</s>, without doubt. (HYP 2.25)

children.text: atha bastiḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Basti</s>:

children.text: nābhi-daghna-jale pāyau nyasta-nālotkaṭāsanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Squatting in water up to the navel, with a tube inserted in the anus, in <s>Utkaṭāsana</s>,

children.text: ādhārākuñcanaṃ kuryāt kṣālanaṃ basti-karma tat // HYP_2.26 //
children.translated_text: one should perform the contraction of the anus — this cleansing is the practice of <s>Basti</s>. (HYP 2.26)

children.text: gulma-plīhodaraṃ cāpi vāta-pitta-kaphodbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Abdominal tumors, diseases of the spleen, and all ailments arising from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> —

children.text: basti-karma-prabhāveṇa kṣīyante sakalāmayāḥ // HYP_2.27 //
children.translated_text: all diseases are destroyed by the power of <s>Basti</s>. (HYP 2.27)

children.text: dhāntvadriyāntaḥ-karaṇa-prasādaṃ
children.translated_text: It bestows clarity of the sense organs and the inner instrument,

children.text: dadhāc ca kāntiṃ dahana-pradīptam /
children.translated_text: grants radiance and kindles the digestive fire,

children.text: aśeṣa-doṣopacayaṃ nihanyād
children.translated_text: destroys the accumulation of all <s>doṣas</s> (imbalances) —

children.text: abhyasyamānaṃ jala-basti-karma // HYP_2.28 //
children.translated_text: the water-<s>Basti</s> practice, when regularly performed. (HYP 2.28)

children.text: atha netiḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Neti</s>:

children.text: sūtraṃ vitasti-susnigdhaṃ nāsānāle praveśayet /
children.translated_text: A smooth thread, a span in length, should be inserted into the nasal passage,

children.text: mukhān nirgamayec caiṣā netiḥ siddhair nigadyate // HYP_2.29 //
children.translated_text: and drawn out through the mouth — this is called <s>Neti</s> by the accomplished ones. (HYP 2.29)

children.text: kapāla-śodhinī caiva divya-dṛṣṭi-pradāyinī /
children.translated_text: It purifies the skull and bestows divine sight,

children.text: jatrūrdhva-jāta-rogaughaṃ netir āśu nihanti ca // HYP_2.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Neti</s> also quickly destroys the host of diseases arising above the shoulders. (HYP 2.30)

children.text: atha trāṭakam-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Trāṭaka</s>:

children.text: nirīkṣen niścala-dṛśā sūkṣma-lakṣyaṃ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should gaze with a steady, unblinking eye at a minute point, with concentration,

children.text: aśru-sampāta-paryantam ācāryais trāṭakaṃ smṛtam // HYP_2.31 //
children.translated_text: until tears flow — this is known by the teachers as <s>Trāṭaka</s>. (HYP 2.31)

children.text: mocanaṃ netra-rogāṇāṃ tandādrīṇāṃ kapāṭakam /
children.translated_text: It is the remedy for eye diseases and the gate that shuts out drowsiness and sloth,

children.text: yatnatas trāṭakaṃ gopyaṃ yathā hāṭaka-peṭakam // HYP_2.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Trāṭaka</s> should be carefully guarded as a secret, like a golden casket. (HYP 2.32)

children.text: atha nauliḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Nauli</s>:

children.text: amandāvarta-vegena tundaṃ savyāpasavyataḥ /
children.translated_text: With a rapid, circular motion, the abdomen should be rotated to the left and right,

children.text: natāṃso bhrāmayed eṣā nauliḥ siddhaiḥ praśasyate // HYP_2.33 //
children.translated_text: with shoulders bent forward — this is <s>Nauli</s>, praised by the accomplished ones. (HYP 2.33)

children.text: mandāgni-sandīpana-pācanādi-sandhāpikānanda-karī sadaiva /
children.translated_text: It kindles the sluggish digestive fire, aids digestion, and so forth, always producing delight,

children.text: aśeṣa-doṣa-maya-śoṣaṇī ca haṭha-kriyā maulir iyaṃ ca nauliḥ // HYP_2.34 //
children.translated_text: it dries up all <s>doṣas</s> and diseases — this <s>Nauli</s> is the crown of <s>Haṭha</s> practices. (HYP 2.34)

children.text: atha kapālabhātiḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Kapālabhāti</s>:

children.text: bhastrāval loha-kārasya reca-pūrau sasambhramau /
children.translated_text: Rapid exhalation and inhalation, like the bellows of a blacksmith —

children.text: kapālabhātir vikhyātā kapha-doṣa-viśoṣaṇī // HYP_2.35 //
children.translated_text: this is known as <s>Kapālabhāti</s>, which dries up disorders of <s>kapha</s>. (HYP 2.35)

children.text: ṣaṭ-karma-nirgata-sthaulya-kapha-doṣa-malādikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having become free from corpulence and <s>kapha</s> impurities through the six actions,

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ tataḥ kuryād anāyāsena siddhyati // HYP_2.36 //
children.translated_text: one should then practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — it is accomplished effortlessly. (HYP 2.36)

children.text: prāṇāyāmair eva sarve praśuṣyanti malā iti /
children.translated_text: Some teachers hold that all impurities are dried up by <s>prāṇāyāma</s> alone,

children.text: ācāryāṇāṃ tu keṣāṃcid anyat karma na saṃmatam // HYP_2.37 //
children.translated_text: and they do not approve of any other practice. (HYP 2.37)

children.text: udara-gata-padārtham udvamanti
children.translated_text: By raising the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) upward and vomiting

children.text: pavanam apānam udīrya kaṇṭha-nāle /
children.translated_text: the contents of the stomach through the throat canal,

children.text: krama-paricaya-vaśya-nāḍi-cakrā
children.translated_text: with the network of <s>nāḍīs</s> brought under control through gradual familiarity —

children.text: gaja-karaṇīti nigadyate haṭhajñaiḥ // HYP_2.38 //
children.translated_text: this is called <s>Gajakaraṇī</s> by those who know <s>Haṭha</s> [yoga]. (HYP 2.38)

children.text: brahmādayo'pi tridaśāḥ pavanābhyāsa-tatparāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods were devoted to the practice of breath [control],

children.text: abhūvann antaka-bhyāt tasmāt pavanam abhyaset // HYP_2.39 //
children.translated_text: out of fear of death — therefore one should practice breath [control]. (HYP 2.39)

children.text: yāvad baddho marud dehe yāvac cittaṃ nirākulam /
children.translated_text: As long as the breath is confined in the body, as long as the mind is undisturbed,

children.text: yāvad dṛṣṭir bhruvor madhye tāvat kāla-bhayaṃ kutaḥ // HYP_2.40 //
children.translated_text: as long as the gaze is fixed between the eyebrows — how then can there be fear of death? (HYP 2.40)

children.text: vidhivat prāṇa-saṃyāmair nāḍī-cakre viśodhite /
children.translated_text: When the network of <s>nāḍīs</s> has been properly purified by the restraint of <s>prāṇa</s>,

children.text: suṣumṇā-vadanaṃ bhittvā sukhād viśati mārutaḥ // HYP_2.41 //
children.translated_text: the breath easily enters the opening of <s>suṣumnā</s>, breaking through it. (HYP 2.41)

children.text: atha manonmanī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Manonmanī</s> (the transcendence of mind):

children.text: mārute madhya-saṃcāre manaḥ-sthairyaṃ prajāyate /
children.translated_text: When the breath moves in the middle [channel], steadiness of mind arises,

children.text: yo manaḥ-susthirī-bhāvaḥ saivāvasthā manonmanī // HYP_2.42 //
children.translated_text: that state of firm steadiness of mind is itself the state of <s>Manonmanī</s>. (HYP 2.42)

children.text: tat-siddhaye vidhānajñāś citrān kurvanti kumbhakān /
children.translated_text: For its accomplishment, those who know the method perform various types of <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention),

children.text: vicitra kumbhakābhyāsād vicitrāṃ siddhim āpnuyāt // HYP_2.43 //
children.translated_text: through the practice of various <s>kumbhakas</s>, one attains various accomplishments. (HYP 2.43)

children.text: atha kumbhaka-bhedāḥ--
children.translated_text: Now, the varieties of <s>kumbhaka</s>:

children.text: sūrya-bhedanam ujjāyī sītkārī śītalī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūryabhedana</s>, <s>Ujjāyī</s>, <s>Sītkārī</s>, <s>Śītalī</s>,

children.text: bhastrikā bhrāmarī mūrcchā plāvinīty aṣṭa-kumbhakāḥ // HYP_2.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhastrikā</s>, <s>Bhrāmarī</s>, <s>Mūrcchā</s>, and <s>Plāvinī</s> — these are the eight <s>kumbhakas</s>. (HYP 2.44)

children.text: pūrakānte tu kartavyo bandho jālandharābhidhaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the end of inhalation, one should perform the lock called <s>Jālandhara</s> (<s>Jālandhara Bandha</s>),

children.text: kumbhakānte recakādau kartavyas tūḍḍiyānakaḥ // HYP_2.45 //
children.translated_text: at the end of retention and the beginning of exhalation, one should perform <s>Uḍḍiyāna</s> (<s>Uḍḍiyāna Bandha</s>). (HYP 2.45)

children.text: adhastāt kuñcanenāśu kaṇṭha-saṅkocane kṛte /
children.translated_text: By the contraction below (<s>Mūla Bandha</s>) and the throat lock performed,

children.text: madhye paścima-tānena syāt prāṇo brahma-nāḍigaḥ // HYP_2.46 //
children.translated_text: with the backward stretch in the middle, the <s>prāṇa</s> enters the <s>Brahma nāḍī</s> (central channel). (HYP 2.46)

children.text: āpānam ūrdhvam utthāpya prāṇaṃ kaṇṭhād adho nayet /
children.translated_text: Raising <s>apāna</s> upward and bringing <s>prāṇa</s> downward from the throat,

children.text: yogī jarā-vimuktaḥ san ṣoḍaśābda-vayā bhavet // HYP_2.47 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s>, freed from old age, becomes as if sixteen years of age. (HYP 2.47)

children.text: atha sūrya-bhedanam-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Sūryabhedana</s> (sun-piercing):

children.text: āsane sukhade yogī baddhvā caivāsanaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s>, seated comfortably, having assumed the posture,

children.text: dakṣa-nāḍyā samākṛṣya bahiḥsthaṃ pavanaṃ śanaiḥ // HYP_2.48 //
children.translated_text: should slowly draw in the external air through the right nostril (<s>dakṣa nāḍī</s>). (HYP 2.48)

children.text: ākeśād ānakhāgrāc ca nirodhāvadhi kumbhayet /
children.translated_text: One should retain [the breath] from the hair to the tips of the nails, until the limit of retention,

children.text: tataḥ śanaiḥ savya-nāḍyā recayet pavanaṃ śanaiḥ // HYP_2.49 //
children.translated_text: then slowly exhale the breath through the left nostril. (HYP 2.49)

children.text: kapāla-śodhanaṃ vāta-doṣa-ghnaṃ kṛmi-doṣa-hṛt /
children.translated_text: It purifies the skull, destroys <s>vāta</s> disorders, and removes parasitic diseases,

children.text: punaḥ punar idaṃ kāryaṃ sūrya-bhedanam uttamam // HYP_2.50 //
children.translated_text: this excellent <s>Sūryabhedana</s> should be practiced again and again. (HYP 2.50)

children.text: atha ujjāyī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Ujjāyī</s> (the victorious breath):

children.text: mukhaṃ saṃyamya nāḍībhyām ākṛṣya pavanaṃ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Closing the mouth, one should slowly draw in the air through both nostrils,

children.text: yathā lagati kaṇṭhāt tu hṛdayāvadhi sa-svanam // HYP_2.51 //
children.translated_text: so that it is felt with a sound from the throat to the heart. (HYP 2.51)

children.text: pūrvavat kumbhayet prāṇaṃ recayed iḍayā tathā /
children.translated_text: One should retain <s>prāṇa</s> as before, and exhale through <s>iḍā</s>,

children.text: śleṣma-doṣa-haraṃ kaṇṭhe dehānala-vivardhanam // HYP_2.52 //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>kapha</s> disorders in the throat and increases the bodily fire. (HYP 2.52)

children.text: nāḍī-jalodarādhātu-gata-doṣa-vināśanam /
children.translated_text: It destroys diseases of the <s>nāḍīs</s>, dropsy, and disorders of the bodily constituents,

children.text: gacchatā tiṣṭhatā kāryam ujjāyy ākhyaṃ tu kumbhakam // HYP_2.53 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kumbhaka</s> called <s>Ujjāyī</s> should be practiced while walking or standing. (HYP 2.53)

children.text: atha sītkārī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Sītkārī</s> (the hissing breath):

children.text: sītkāṃ kuryāt tathā vaktre ghrāṇenaiva vijṛmbhikām /
children.translated_text: One should make a hissing sound with the mouth and exhale only through the nostrils,

children.text: evam abhyāsa-yogena kāma-devo dvitīyakaḥ // HYP_2.54 //
children.translated_text: by this practice, one becomes a second <s>Kāmadeva</s> (god of love). (HYP 2.54)

children.text: yoginī cakra-saṃmānyaḥ sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra-kārakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Honored by the circle of <s>yoginīs</s>, capable of creation and dissolution,

children.text: na kṣudhā na tṛṣā nidrā naivālasyaṃ prajāyate // HYP_2.55 //
children.translated_text: neither hunger, nor thirst, nor sleep, nor laziness arises. (HYP 2.55)

children.text: bhavet sattvaṃ ca dehasya sarvopadrava-varjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> (purity) of the body increases, and one becomes free from all afflictions,

children.text: anena vidhinā satyaṃ yogīndro bhūmi-maṇḍale // HYP_2.56 //
children.translated_text: by this method, truly, one becomes the lord of <s>yogīs</s> on the earthly plane. (HYP 2.56)

children.text: atha śītalī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Śītalī</s> (the cooling breath):

children.text: jihvayā vāyum ākṛṣya pūrvavat kumbha-sādhanam /
children.translated_text: Drawing air in through the tongue, one performs <s>kumbhaka</s> as before,

children.text: śanakair ghrāṇa-randhrābhyāṃ recayet pavanaṃ sudhīḥ // HYP_2.57 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should slowly exhale through both nostrils. (HYP 2.57)

children.text: gulma-plīhādikān rogān jvaraṃ pittaṃ kṣudhāṃ tṛṣām /
children.translated_text: Abdominal tumors, diseases of the spleen, fever, <s>pitta</s>, hunger, thirst,

children.text: viṣāṇi śītalī nāma kumbhikeyaṃ nihanti hi // HYP_2.58 //
children.translated_text: and poisons — this <s>kumbhaka</s> called <s>Śītalī</s> indeed destroys all these. (HYP 2.58)

children.text: atha bhastrikā-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Bhastrikā</s> (the bellows breath):

children.text: ūrvor upari saṃsthāpya śubhe pāda-tale ubhe /
children.translated_text: Placing both feet upon the thighs,

children.text: padmāsanaṃ bhaved etat sarva-pāpa-praṇāśanam // HYP_2.59 //
children.translated_text: this is <s>Padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), which destroys all sins. (HYP 2.59)

children.text: samyak padmāsanaṃ baddhvā sama-grīvodaraḥ sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Having properly assumed <s>Padmāsana</s>, with neck and abdomen aligned, the wise one

children.text: mukhaṃ saṃyamya yatnena prāṇaṃ ghrāṇena recayet // HYP_2.60 //
children.translated_text: should close the mouth and carefully exhale through the nose. (HYP 2.60)

children.text: yathā lagati hṛt-kaṇṭhe kapālāvadhi sa-svanam /
children.translated_text: So that it is felt with sound from the heart and throat up to the skull,

children.text: vegena pūrayec cāpi hṛt-padmāvadhi mārutam // HYP_2.61 //
children.translated_text: and then one should rapidly fill with air up to the heart-lotus. (HYP 2.61)

children.text: punar virecayet tadvat pūrayec ca punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Again one should exhale in the same way, and fill again and again,

children.text: yathaiva lohakāreṇa bhastrā vegena cālyate // HYP_2.62 //
children.translated_text: just as the bellows of a blacksmith are rapidly operated. (HYP 2.62)

children.text: tathaiva sva-śarīra-sthaṃ cālayet pavanaṃ dhiyā /
children.translated_text: In the same way, one should move the breath within one's own body with awareness,

children.text: yadā śramo bhaved dehe tadā sūryeṇa pūrayet // HYP_2.63 //
children.translated_text: when fatigue arises in the body, one should then inhale through the right nostril. (HYP 2.63)

children.text: yathodaraṃ bhavet pūrṇam anilena tathā laghu /
children.translated_text: When the abdomen is fully filled with air and feels light,

children.text: dhārayen nāsikāṃ madhyā-tarjanībhyāṃ vinā dṛḍham // HYP_2.64 //
children.translated_text: one should firmly hold the nostrils with the middle and index fingers. (HYP 2.64)

children.text: vidhivat kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā recayed iḍayānilam /
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>kumbhaka</s> according to the prescribed method, one should exhale through <s>iḍā</s>,

children.text: vāta-pitta-śleṣma-haraṃ śarīrāgni-vivardhanam // HYP_2.65 //
children.translated_text: it removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and increases the bodily fire. (HYP 2.65)

children.text: kuṇḍalī bodhakaṃ kṣipraṃ pavanaṃ sukhadaṃ hitam /
children.translated_text: It quickly awakens <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, is pleasant and beneficial,

children.text: brahma-nāḍī-mukhe saṃstha-kaphādy-argala-nāśanam // HYP_2.66 //
children.translated_text: it destroys the obstructions of <s>kapha</s> and other [impurities] at the entrance of the <s>Brahma nāḍī</s>. (HYP 2.66)

children.text: samyag gātra-samudbhūta-granthi-traya-vibhedakam /
children.translated_text: It effectively breaks through the three knots (<s>granthis</s>) formed in the body,

children.text: viśeṣeṇaiva kartavyaṃ bhastrākhyaṃ kumbhakaṃ tv idam // HYP_2.67 //
children.translated_text: this <s>kumbhaka</s> called <s>Bhastrikā</s> should be practiced with special diligence. (HYP 2.67)

children.text: vegād ghoṣaṃ pūrakaṃ bhṛṅga-nādaṃ
children.translated_text: Inhaling rapidly with the buzzing sound of a male bee,

children.text: bhṛṅgī-nādaṃ recakaṃ manda-mandam /
children.translated_text: and exhaling slowly with the buzzing sound of a female bee,

children.text: yogīndrāṇī̀am evam abhyāsa-yogāc
children.translated_text: through this practice, for the lords of <s>yogīs</s>,

children.text: citte jātā kācid ānanda-līlā // HYP_2.68 //
children.translated_text: a certain play of bliss arises in the mind. (HYP 2.68)

children.text: atha mūrcchā-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Mūrcchā</s> (the swooning breath):

children.text: pūrakānte gāḍhataraṃ baddhvā jālandharaṃ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: At the end of inhalation, having firmly applied <s>Jālandhara Bandha</s>, one should slowly

children.text: recayen mūrcchākhyeyaṃ mano-mūrcchā sukha-pradā // HYP_2.69 //
children.translated_text: exhale — this is called <s>Mūrcchā</s>, the swooning [breath] that bestows bliss. (HYP 2.69)

children.text: atha plāvinī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Plāvinī</s> (the floating breath):

children.text: antaḥ pravartitodāra-mārutāpūritodaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having filled the interior of the abdomen abundantly with air drawn in,

children.text: payasy agādhe'pi sukhāt plavate padma-patravat // HYP_2.70 //
children.translated_text: one floats easily, even in deep water, like a lotus leaf. (HYP 2.70)

children.text: prāṇāyāmas tridhā prokto reca-pūraka-kumbhakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> is declared to be threefold: exhalation, inhalation, and retention,

children.text: sahitaḥ kevalaś ceti kumbhako dvividho mataḥ // HYP_2.71 //
children.translated_text: and <s>kumbhaka</s> is considered to be of two kinds: <s>sahita</s> (combined) and <s>kevala</s> (absolute). (HYP 2.71)

children.text: yāvat kevala-siddhiḥ syāt sahitaṃ tāvad abhyaset /
children.translated_text: One should practice <s>sahita</s> until <s>kevala siddhi</s> (mastery of absolute retention) is attained,

children.text: recakaṃ pūrakaṃ muktvā sukhaṃ yad vāyu-dhāraṇam // HYP_2.72 //
children.translated_text: the comfortable retention of breath, free from exhalation and inhalation — (HYP 2.72)

children.text: prāṇāyāmo'yam ity uktaḥ sa vai kevala-kumbhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: this is called <s>prāṇāyāma</s>; it is indeed <s>kevala kumbhaka</s> (absolute retention),

children.text: kumbhake kevale siddhe reca-pūraka-varjite // HYP_2.73 //
children.translated_text: when <s>kevala kumbhaka</s> is mastered, free from exhalation and inhalation, (HYP 2.73)

children.text: na tasya durlabhaṃ kiṃcit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate /
children.translated_text: nothing in the three worlds is unattainable for him,

children.text: śaktaḥ kevala-kumbhena yatheṣṭaṃ vāyu-dhāraṇāt // HYP_2.74 //
children.translated_text: one who is capable of <s>kevala kumbhaka</s>, of retaining breath at will. (HYP 2.74)

children.text: rāja-yoga-padaṃ cāpi labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: He also attains the state of <s>Rāja Yoga</s> — in this there is no doubt,

children.text: kumbhakāt kuṇḍalī-bodhaḥ kuṇḍalī-bodhato bhavet /
children.translated_text: from <s>kumbhaka</s> arises the awakening of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>; from the awakening of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>,

children.text: anargalā suṣumṇā ca haṭha-siddhiś ca jāyate // HYP_2.75 //
children.translated_text: the <s>suṣumnā</s> becomes unobstructed, and the accomplishment of <s>Haṭha</s> [yoga] arises. (HYP 2.75)

children.text: haṭhaṃ vinā rājayogo rāja-yogaṃ vinā haṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without <s>Haṭha</s>, <s>Rāja Yoga</s> [cannot succeed], and without <s>Rāja Yoga</s>, <s>Haṭha</s> [cannot succeed],

children.text: na sidhyati tato yugmam āniṣpatteḥ samabhyaset // HYP_2.76 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should practice both together until perfection is attained. (HYP 2.76)

children.text: kumbhaka-prāṇa-rodhānte kuryāc cittaṃ nirāśrayam /
children.translated_text: At the end of the restraint of breath through <s>kumbhaka</s>, one should make the mind supportless,

children.text: evam abhyāsa-yogena rāja-yoga-padaṃ vrajet // HYP_2.77 //
children.translated_text: by this practice, one attains the state of <s>Rāja Yoga</s>. (HYP 2.77)

children.text: vapuḥ kṛśatvaṃ vadane prasannatā
children.translated_text: Leanness of body, cheerfulness of face,

children.text: nāda-sphuṭatvaṃ nayane sunirmale /
children.translated_text: clarity of the inner sound (<s>nāda</s>), eyes very clear,

children.text: arogatā bindu-jayo'gni-dīpanaṃ
children.translated_text: freedom from disease, mastery over <s>bindu</s> (seminal energy), kindling of the digestive fire,

children.text: nāḍī-viśuddhir haṭha-siddhi-lakṣaṇam // HYP_2.78 //
children.translated_text: and purity of the <s>nāḍīs</s> — these are the signs of accomplishment in <s>Haṭha</s> [yoga]. (HYP 2.78)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter of the <s>Haṭhapradīpikā</s>.

children.text: sa-śaila-vana-dhātrīṇāṃ yathādhāro'hi-nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the king of serpents is the support of the earth with its mountains and forests,

children.text: sarveṣāṃ yoga-tantrāṇāṃ tathādhāro hi kuṇḍalī // HYP_3.1 //
children.translated_text: so <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> is the support of all <s>yoga tantras</s> (yoga systems). (HYP 3.1)

children.text: suptā guru-prasādena yadā jāgarti kuṇḍalī /
children.translated_text: When the sleeping <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> is awakened by the grace of the <s>guru</s>,

children.text: tadā sarvāṇi padmāni bhidyante granthayo'pi ca // HYP_3.2 //
children.translated_text: then all the lotuses (<s>cakras</s>) are pierced, and the knots (<s>granthis</s>) too. // HYP 3.2 //

children.text: prāṇasya śūnya-padavī tadā rājapathāyate /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>suṣumnā</s> becomes the royal path for the <s>prāṇa</s>'s passage through the void,

children.text: tadā cittaṃ nirālambaṃ tadā kālasya vañcanam // HYP_3.3 //
children.translated_text: then the mind becomes supportless, and then there is the deception of death. // HYP 3.3 //

children.text: suṣumṇā śūnya-padavī brahma-randhraḥ mahāpathaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣumnā</s>, the void-path, <s>brahmarandhra</s> (the aperture of Brahman), the great path,

children.text: śmaśānaṃ śāmbhavī madhya-mārgaś cety eka-vācakāḥ // HYP_3.4 //
children.translated_text: the cremation ground, <s>śāmbhavī</s>, the central channel — these are synonymous terms. // HYP 3.4 //

children.text: tasmāt sarva-prayatnena prabodhayitum īśvarīm /
children.translated_text: Therefore, with all effort, to awaken the <s>Īśvarī</s> (Goddess, i.e. Kuṇḍalinī)

children.text: brahma-dvāra-mukhe suptāṃ mudrābhyāsaṃ samācaret // HYP_3.5 //
children.translated_text: sleeping at the mouth of the door of <s>Brahman</s>, one should practice <s>mudrā</s>. // HYP 3.5 //

children.text: mahāmudrā mahābandho mahāvedhaś ca khecarī /
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (the great seal), <s>mahābandha</s> (the great lock), <s>mahāvedha</s> (the great piercing), and <s>khecarī</s> (the space-moving seal),

children.text: uḍḍīyānaṃ mūlabandhaś ca bandho jālandharābhidhaḥ // HYP_3.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>uḍḍīyāna</s> (the flying-up lock), <s>mūlabandha</s> (the root lock), and the lock called <s>jālandhara</s>, // HYP 3.6 //

children.text: karaṇī viparītākhyā vajrolī śakti-cālanam /
children.translated_text: <s>viparītakaraṇī</s> (the inverted action), <s>vajrolī</s>, and <s>śakticālana</s> (the stirring of energy) —

children.text: idaṃ hi mudrā-daśakaṃ jarā-maraṇa-nāśanam // HYP_3.7 //
children.translated_text: these are the ten <s>mudrās</s> which destroy old age and death. // HYP 3.7 //

children.text: ādināthoditaṃ divyam aṣṭaiśvarya-pradāyakam /
children.translated_text: Taught by the Primordial Lord (<s>Ādinātha</s>), they are divine and bestow the eight supernatural powers (<s>aṣṭaiśvarya</s>);

children.text: vallabhaṃ sarva-siddhānāṃ durlabhaṃ marutām api // HYP_3.8 //
children.translated_text: they are dear to all <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones) and difficult to attain even by the gods (<s>Maruts</s>). // HYP 3.8 //

children.text: gopanīyaṃ prayatnena yathā ratna-karaṇḍakam /
children.translated_text: They should be carefully kept secret, like a casket of jewels;

children.text: kasyacin naiva vaktavyaṃ kula-strī-surataṃ yathā // HYP_3.9 //
children.translated_text: they should not be told to anyone, just as the sexual union with a respectable woman (is not discussed). // HYP 3.9 //

children.text: atha mahā-mudrā-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (the Great Seal):

children.text: pāda-mūlena vāmena yoniṃ sampīḍya dakṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: Pressing the perineum (<s>yoni</s>) with the heel of the left foot, the right (leg)

children.text: prasāritaṃ padaṃ kṛtvā karābhyāṃ dhārayed dṛḍham // HYP_3.10 //
children.translated_text: being extended, one should firmly hold (the toe of the right foot) with both hands. // HYP 3.10 //

children.text: kaṇṭhe bandhaṃ samāropya dhārayed vāyum ūrdhvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Applying the throat lock (<s>kaṇṭhabandha</s>), one should hold the breath upward;

children.text: yathā daṇḍa-hataḥ sarpo daṇḍākāraḥ prajāyate // HYP_3.11 //
children.translated_text: just as a snake struck by a stick becomes straight like a rod, // HYP 3.11 //

children.text: ṛjvībhūtā tathā śaktiḥ kuṇḍalī sahasā bhavet /
children.translated_text: so the energy (<s>śakti</s>), the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, suddenly becomes straight.

children.text: tadā sā maraṇāvasthā jāyate dvipuṭāśrayā // HYP_3.12 //
children.translated_text: Then a death-like state arises in the two-petaled (lotus, i.e. <s>ājñā cakra</s>). // HYP 3.12 //

children.text: tataḥ śanaiḥ śanair eva recayen naiva vegataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then one should exhale very slowly, not forcefully;

children.text: mahā-mudrāṃ ca tenaiva vadanti vibudhottamāḥ // HYP_3.13 //
children.translated_text: for this reason the greatest sages call it <s>Mahāmudrā</s>. // HYP 3.13 //

children.text: iyaṃ khalu mahāmudrā mahā-siddhaiḥ pradarśitā /
children.translated_text: This <s>Mahāmudrā</s> has been demonstrated by the great <s>siddhas</s>;

children.text: mahā-kleśādayo doṣāḥ kṣīyante maraṇādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: great afflictions (<s>mahākleśas</s>) and other faults such as death are destroyed;

children.text: mahā-mudrāṃ ca tenaiva vadanti vibudhottamāḥ // HYP_3.14 //
children.translated_text: for this reason the greatest sages call it <s>Mahāmudrā</s>. // HYP 3.14 //

children.text: candrāṅge tu samabhyasya sūryāṅge punar abhyaset /
children.translated_text: Having practiced on the left side (moon side), one should then practice on the right side (sun side);

children.text: yāvat-tulyā bhavet saṅkhyā tato mudrāṃ visarjayet // HYP_3.15 //
children.translated_text: when the count becomes equal, one should release the <s>mudrā</s>. // HYP 3.15 //

children.text: na hi pathyam apathyaṃ vā rasāḥ sarve'pi nīrasāḥ /
children.translated_text: There is neither wholesome nor unwholesome food (for the practitioner); all tastes become tasteless;

children.text: api bhuktaṃ viṣaṃ ghoraṃ pīyūṣam api jīryati // HYP_3.16 //
children.translated_text: even terrible poison when consumed is digested like nectar. // HYP 3.16 //

children.text: kṣaya-kuṣṭha-gudāvarta-gulmājīrṇa-purogamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Consumption, leprosy, constipation, abdominal tumors, indigestion, and other

children.text: tasya doṣāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti mahāmudrāṃ tu yo'bhyaset // HYP_3.17 //
children.translated_text: diseases are destroyed for one who practices <s>Mahāmudrā</s>. // HYP 3.17 //

children.text: kathiteyaṃ mahāmudrā mahā-siddhi-karā nṝṇām /
children.translated_text: This <s>Mahāmudrā</s> has been described as the bestower of great <s>siddhis</s> for humans;

children.text: gopanīyā prayatnena na deyā yasya kasyacit // HYP_3.18 //
children.translated_text: it should be carefully kept secret and not given to just anyone. // HYP 3.18 //

children.text: atha mahā-bandhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Mahābandha</s> (the Great Lock):

children.text: pārṣṇiṃ vāmasya pādasya yoni-sthāne niyojayet /
children.translated_text: One should place the heel of the left foot at the perineum (<s>yonisthāna</s>),

children.text: vāmorūpari saṃsthāpya dakṣiṇaṃ caraṇaṃ tathā // HYP_3.19 //
children.translated_text: and likewise place the right foot upon the left thigh. // HYP 3.19 //

children.text: pūrayitvā tato vāyuṃ hṛdaye cubukaṃ dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Then, having filled (the lungs) with breath, firmly pressing the chin to the chest,

children.text: niṣpīḍyaṃ vāyum ākuñcya mano-madhye niyojayet // HYP_3.20 //
children.translated_text: contracting the breath, one should fix (the mind) in the center. // HYP 3.20 //

children.text: dhārayitvā yathā-śakti recayed anilaṃ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having retained as long as possible, one should exhale the breath slowly;

children.text: savyāṅge tu samabhyasya dakṣāṅge punar abhyaset // HYP_3.21 //
children.translated_text: having practiced on the left side, one should then practice on the right side. // HYP 3.21 //

children.text: matam atra tu keṣāṃcit kaṇṭha-bandhaṃ vivarjayet /
children.translated_text: The opinion of some here is that the throat lock should be omitted;

children.text: rāja-danta-stha-jihvāyā bandhaḥ śasto bhaved iti // HYP_3.22 //
children.translated_text: the lock with the tongue pressed against the front teeth is considered excellent. // HYP 3.22 //

children.text: ayaṃ tu sarva-nāḍīnām ūrdhvaṃ gati-nirodhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: This (lock) blocks the upward movement of all the <s>nāḍīs</s>;

children.text: ayaṃ khalu mahā-bandho mahā-siddhi-pradāyakaḥ // HYP_3.23 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Mahābandha</s> is indeed the bestower of great <s>siddhis</s>. // HYP 3.23 //

children.text: kāla-pāśa-mahā-bandha-vimocana-vicakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is skilled in liberating from the great snare of the noose of Time (<s>Kāla</s>);

children.text: triveṇī-saṅgamaṃ dhatte kedāraṃ prāpayen manaḥ // HYP_3.24 //
children.translated_text: it brings about the confluence of the three rivers (<s>triveṇī</s>) and enables the mind to reach <s>Kedāra</s>. // HYP 3.24 //

children.text: rūpa-lāvaṇya-sampannā yathā strī puruṣaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: Just as a woman endowed with beauty and grace is useless without a man,

children.text: mahā-mudrā-mahā-bandhau niṣphalau vedha-varjitau // HYP_3.25 //
children.translated_text: so <s>Mahāmudrā</s> and <s>Mahābandha</s> are fruitless without the piercing (<s>vedha</s>). // HYP 3.25 //

children.text: atha mahā-vedhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Mahāvedha</s> (the Great Piercing):

children.text: mahā-bandha-sthito yogī kṛtvā pūrakam eka-dhīḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s>, seated in <s>Mahābandha</s>, having performed inhalation with concentrated mind,

children.text: vāyūnāṃ gatim āvṛtya nibhṛtaṃ kaṇṭha-mudrayā // HYP_3.26 //
children.translated_text: blocking the movement of the vital airs firmly with the throat seal (<s>kaṇṭhamudrā</s>), // HYP 3.26 //

children.text: sama-hasta-yugo bhūmau sphicau sanāḍayec chanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with both hands placed evenly on the ground, should gently raise the buttocks and tap (them);

children.text: puṭa-dvayam atikramya vāyuḥ sphurati madhyagaḥ // HYP_3.27 //
children.translated_text: passing beyond the two openings, the breath pulsates in the central (channel). // HYP 3.27 //

children.text: soma-sūryāgni-sambandho jāyate cāmṛtāya vai /
children.translated_text: The conjunction of moon, sun, and fire arises indeed for the sake of immortality;

children.text: mṛtāvasthā samutpannā tato vāyuṃ virecayet // HYP_3.28 //
children.translated_text: a death-like state is produced — then one should release the breath. // HYP 3.28 //

children.text: mahā-vedho'yam abhyāsān mahā-siddhi-pradāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>Mahāvedha</s>, through practice, is the bestower of great <s>siddhis</s>;

children.text: valī-palita-vepa-ghnaḥ sevyate sādhakottamaiḥ // HYP_3.29 //
children.translated_text: it destroys wrinkles, grey hair, and trembling, and is practiced by the best of practitioners. // HYP 3.29 //

children.text: etat trayaṃ mahā-guhyaṃ jarā-mṛtyu-vināśanam /
children.translated_text: These three are the great secrets, destroyers of old age and death,

children.text: vahni-vṛddhi-karaṃ caiva hy aṇimādi-guṇa-pradam // HYP_3.30 //
children.translated_text: and they increase the digestive fire and bestow qualities such as <s>aṇimā</s> (the power of becoming minute). // HYP 3.30 //

children.text: aṣṭadhā kriyate caiva yāme yāme dine dine /
children.translated_text: They should be performed eight times daily, at each watch (<s>yāma</s>), day by day;

children.text: puṇya-saṃbhāra-sandhāya pāpaugha-bhiduraṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: they always accumulate merit and shatter the mass of sins;

children.text: samyak-śikṣāvatām evaṃ svalpaṃ prathama-sādhanam // HYP_3.31 //
children.translated_text: for those properly instructed, even a little practice in the beginning (yields results). // HYP 3.31 //

children.text: atha khecarī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Khecarī</s> (the Space-Moving Seal):

children.text: kapāla-kuhare jihvā praviṣṭā viparītagā /
children.translated_text: When the tongue enters the cavity of the skull, turned upward,

children.text: bhruvor antargatā dṛṣṭir mudrā bhavati khecarī // HYP_3.32 //
children.translated_text: and the gaze is fixed between the eyebrows — this becomes <s>Khecarī mudrā</s>. // HYP 3.32 //

children.text: chedana-cālana-dohaiḥ kalāṃ krameṇātha vardhayet tāvat /
children.translated_text: Through cutting, moving, and milking, one should gradually lengthen the tongue (<s>kalā</s>),

children.text: sā yāvad bhrū-madhyaṃ spṛśati tadā khecarī-siddhiḥ // HYP_3.33 //
children.translated_text: until it touches the space between the eyebrows — then <s>Khecarī siddhi</s> is attained. // HYP 3.33 //

children.text: snuhī-patra-nibhaṃ śastraṃ sutīkṣṇaṃ snigdha-nirmalam /
children.translated_text: Taking a sharp, smooth, clean instrument resembling a <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) leaf,

children.text: samādāya tatas tena roma-mātraṃ samucchinet // HYP_3.34 //
children.translated_text: with that, one should cut a hair's breadth (of the frenulum). // HYP 3.34 //

children.text: tataḥ saindhava-pathyābhyāṃ cūrṇitābhyāṃ pragharṣayet /
children.translated_text: Then one should rub it with powdered rock salt and <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan);

children.text: punaḥ sapta-dine prāpte roma-mātraṃ samucchinet // HYP_3.35 //
children.translated_text: again, after seven days, one should cut a hair's breadth. // HYP 3.35 //

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa ṣaṇ-māsaṃ nityaṃ yuktaḥ samācaret /
children.translated_text: Thus, gradually, for six months, one should diligently practice;

children.text: ṣaṇmāsād rasanā-mūla-śirā-bandhaḥ praṇaśyati // HYP_3.36 //
children.translated_text: in six months, the binding vein at the root of the tongue is destroyed. // HYP 3.36 //

children.text: kalāṃ parāṅmukhīṃ kṛtvā tripathe pariyojayet /
children.translated_text: Having turned the tongue upward, one should insert it at the junction of the three paths;

children.text: sā bhavet khecarī mudrā vyoma-cakraṃ tad ucyate // HYP_3.37 //
children.translated_text: this becomes <s>Khecarī mudrā</s> — it is called the sky-wheel (<s>vyomacakra</s>). // HYP 3.37 //

children.text: rasanām ūrdhvagāṃ kṛtvā kṣaṇārdham api tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: One who keeps the tongue turned upward even for half a moment

children.text: viṣair vimucyate yogī vyādhi-mṛtyu-jarādibhiḥ // HYP_3.38 //
children.translated_text: is freed from poisons — the <s>yogin</s> is freed from diseases, death, old age, and the rest. // HYP 3.38 //

children.text: na rogo maraṇaṃ tandrā na nidrā na kṣudhā tṛṣā /
children.translated_text: There is no disease, no death, no drowsiness, no sleep, no hunger, no thirst,

children.text: na ca mūrcchā bhavet tasya yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm // HYP_3.39 //
children.translated_text: nor fainting for one who knows <s>Khecarī mudrā</s>. // HYP 3.39 //

children.text: pīḍyate na sa rogeṇa lipyate na ca karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: He is not afflicted by disease, nor tainted by <s>karma</s>,

children.text: bādhyate na sa kālena yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm // HYP_3.40 //
children.translated_text: nor bound by time — one who knows <s>Khecarī mudrā</s>. // HYP 3.40 //

children.text: cittaṃ carati khe yasmāj jihvā carati khe gatā /
children.translated_text: Because the mind moves in space (<s>kha</s>), and the tongue also moves in space (the palatal cavity),

children.text: tenaiṣā khecarī nāma mudrā siddhair nirūpitā // HYP_3.41 //
children.translated_text: therefore this <s>mudrā</s> is called <s>Khecarī</s> (space-moving) — thus defined by the <s>siddhas</s>. // HYP 3.41 //

children.text: khecaryā mudritaṃ yena vivaraṃ lambikordhvataḥ /
children.translated_text: For one whose opening above the <s>lambikā</s> (uvula) is sealed by <s>Khecarī</s>,

children.text: na tasya kṣarate binduḥ kāminyāḥ śleṣitasya ca // HYP_3.42 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bindu</s> (seminal essence) does not flow out, even when embraced by a woman. // HYP 3.42 //

children.text: calito'pi yadā binduḥ samprāpto yoni-maṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: Even when the <s>bindu</s> has moved and reached the region of the <s>yoni</s>,

children.text: vrajaty ūrdhvaṃ hṛtaḥ śaktyā nibaddho yoni-mudrayā // HYP_3.43 //
children.translated_text: it goes upward, drawn by the <s>śakti</s> (energy), held by <s>yonimudrā</s>. // HYP 3.43 //

children.text: ūrdhva-jihvaḥ sthiro bhūtvā somapānaṃ karoti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who, with the tongue turned upward, remains steady and drinks the lunar nectar (<s>somapāna</s>),

children.text: māsārdhena na sandeho mṛtyuṃ jayati yogavit // HYP_3.44 //
children.translated_text: within half a month, without doubt, the knower of <s>yoga</s> conquers death. // HYP 3.44 //

children.text: nityaṃ soma-kalā-pūrṇaṃ śarīraṃ yasya yoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body of the <s>yogin</s> that is always filled with the lunar nectar (<s>somakalā</s>),

children.text: takṣakeṇāpi daṣṭasya viṣaṃ tasya na sarpati // HYP_3.45 //
children.translated_text: even if bitten by <s>Takṣaka</s> (the serpent king), the poison does not spread in him. // HYP 3.45 //

children.text: indhanāni yathā vahnis taila-varti ca dīpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as fire (does not leave) fuel, and the lamp (does not leave) the oil-wick,
