children.text: tathā soma-kalā-pūrṇaṃ dehī dehaṃ na muñcati // HYP_3.46 //
children.translated_text: so the embodied soul does not leave the body filled with the lunar nectar. // HYP 3.46 //

children.text: gomāṃsaṃ bhakṣayen nityaṃ pibed amara-vāruṇīm /
children.translated_text: One should daily eat 'cow-flesh' and drink the 'immortal wine';

children.text: kulīnaṃ tam ahaṃ manye cetare kula-ghātakāḥ // HYP_3.47 //
children.translated_text: I consider him of noble birth — the rest are destroyers of their lineage. // HYP 3.47 //

children.text: go-śabdenoditā jihvā tat praveśo hi tāluni /
children.translated_text: By the word 'go' (cow) the tongue is indicated; its entry into the palate

children.text: go-māṃsa-bhakṣaṇaṃ tat tu mahā-pātaka-nāśanam // HYP_3.48 //
children.translated_text: is the eating of 'cow-flesh' — that indeed destroys great sins. // HYP 3.48 //

children.text: jihvā-praveśa-sambhūta-vahninotpāditaḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: The essence that flows from the moon, produced by the fire generated

children.text: candrāt sravati yaḥ sāraḥ sā syād amara-vāruṇī // HYP_3.49 //
children.translated_text: from the entry of the tongue (into the palate) — that is the 'immortal wine.' // HYP 3.49 //

children.text: cumbantī yadi lambikāgram aniśaṃ jihvā-rasa-syandinī
children.translated_text: When the tongue constantly kisses the tip of the <s>lambikā</s> (uvula), dripping with nectar,

children.text: sa-kṣārā kaṭukāmla-dugdha-sadṛśī madhvājya-tulyā tathā /
children.translated_text: salty, pungent, sour, like milk, like honey and ghee,

children.text: vyādhīnāṃ haraṇaṃ jarānta-karaṇaṃ śastrāgamodīraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: the destruction of diseases, the ending of old age, the arousing of weapons and scriptures,

children.text: tasya syād amaratvam aṣṭa-guṇitaṃ siddhāṅganākarṣaṇam // HYP_3.50 //
children.translated_text: immortality, the eightfold (powers), and the attraction of <s>siddha</s>-women — all these become his. // HYP 3.50 //

children.text: mūrdhnaḥ ṣoḍaśa-patra-padma-galitaṃ prāṇād avāptaṃ haṭhād
children.translated_text: The nectar flowing from the sixteen-petaled lotus at the crown, obtained by <s>prāṇa</s> through <s>haṭha</s>,

children.text: ūrdvhāsyo rasanāṃ niyamya vivare śaktiṃ parāṃ cintayan /
children.translated_text: with face turned upward, restraining the tongue in the cavity, contemplating the supreme <s>śakti</s>,

children.text: utkallola-kalā-jalaṃ ca vimalaṃ dhārāmayaṃ yaḥ piben
children.translated_text: one who drinks the pure, streaming, wave-crested nectar —

children.text: nirvyādhiḥ sa mṛṇāla-komala-vapur yogī ciraṃ jīvati // HYP_3.51 //
children.translated_text: that <s>yogin</s>, free from disease, with a body soft as a lotus stalk, lives long. // HYP 3.51 //

children.text: yat prāleyaṃ prahita-suṣiraṃ meru-mūrdhāntara-sthaṃ
children.translated_text: That which is cool, perforated, and situated at the summit of <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: tasmiṃs tattvaṃ pravadati sudhīs tan-mukhaṃ nimnagānām /
children.translated_text: the wise person declares that reality to be the source of rivers (nāḍīs);

children.text: candrāt sāraḥ sravati vapuṣas tena mṛtyur narāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: from the moon the essence flows through the body — thereby death comes to humans;

children.text: tad badhnīyāt sukaraṇam adho nānyathā kāya-siddhiḥ // HYP_3.52 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should bind it (the nectar) skillfully below — there is no other way to bodily perfection (<s>kāyasiddhi</s>). // HYP 3.52 //

children.text: suṣiraṃ jñāna-janakaṃ pañca-srotaḥ-samanvitam /
children.translated_text: The cavity that generates knowledge, endowed with five streams —

children.text: tiṣṭhate khecarī mudrā tasmin śūnye nirañjane // HYP_3.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khecarī mudrā</s> abides in that stainless void. // HYP 3.53 //

children.text: ekaṃ sṛṣṭimayaṃ bījam ekā mudrā ca khecarī /
children.translated_text: One seed that contains creation, one <s>mudrā</s> — <s>Khecarī</s>,

children.text: eko devo nirālamba ekāvasthā manonmanī // HYP_3.54 //
children.translated_text: one God without support, one state — <s>Manonmanī</s> (the state beyond mind). // HYP 3.54 //

children.text: atha uḍḍīyāna-bandhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Uḍḍīyāna Bandha</s> (the Flying-Up Lock):

children.text: baddho yena suṣumṇāyāṃ prāṇas tūḍḍīyate yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the <s>prāṇa</s>, bound in the <s>suṣumnā</s>, flies upward through this,

children.text: tasmād uḍḍīyanākhyo'yaṃ yogibhiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ // HYP_3.55 //
children.translated_text: therefore this is called <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s> (flying up) by the <s>yogins</s>. // HYP 3.55 //

children.text: uḍḍīnaṃ kurute yasmād aviśrāntaṃ mahā-khagaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the great bird (of <s>prāṇa</s>) flies up ceaselessly through it,

children.text: uḍḍīyānaṃ tad eva syāt tava bandho'bhidhīyate // HYP_3.56 //
children.translated_text: that itself is <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s> — thus your lock is described. // HYP 3.56 //

children.text: udare paścimaṃ tānaṃ nābher ūrdhvaṃ ca kārayet /
children.translated_text: One should draw the abdomen backward and upward above the navel;

children.text: uḍḍīyāno hy asau bandho mṛtyu-mātaṅga-kesarī // HYP_3.57 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Uḍḍīyāna bandha</s> is the lion that slays the elephant of death. // HYP 3.57 //

children.text: uḍḍīyānaṃ tu sahajaṃ guruṇā kathitaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s>, which is natural, should always be practiced as taught by the <s>guru</s>;

children.text: abhyaset satataṃ yas tu vṛddho'pi taruṇāyate // HYP_3.58 //
children.translated_text: one who practices it constantly becomes youthful even when old. // HYP 3.58 //

children.text: nābher ūrdhvam adhaś cāpi tānaṃ kuryāt prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: One should carefully draw upward and downward the region above and below the navel;

children.text: ṣaṇmāsam abhyasen mṛtyuṃ jayaty eva na saṃśayaḥ // HYP_3.59 //
children.translated_text: practicing for six months, one certainly conquers death — there is no doubt. // HYP 3.59 //

children.text: sarveṣām eva bandhānāṃ uttamo hy uḍḍīyānakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of all the <s>bandhas</s>, <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s> is indeed the best;

children.text: uḍḍiyāne dṛḍhe bandhe muktiḥ svābhāvikī bhavet // HYP_3.60 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Uḍḍīyāna bandha</s> is firmly established, liberation occurs naturally. // HYP 3.60 //

children.text: atha mūla-bandhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Mūla Bandha</s> (the Root Lock):

children.text: pārṣṇi-bhāgena sampīḍya yonim ākuñcayed gudam /
children.translated_text: Pressing the perineum (<s>yoni</s>) with the heel, one should contract the anus (<s>guda</s>);

children.text: apānam ūrdhvam ākṛṣya mūla-bandho'bhidhīyate // HYP_3.61 //
children.translated_text: drawing the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) upward — this is called <s>Mūla bandha</s>. // HYP 3.61 //

children.text: adho-gatim apānaṃ vā ūrdhvagaṃ kurute balāt /
children.translated_text: The <s>apāna</s>, whose natural movement is downward, is forcefully made to go upward;

children.text: ākuñcanena taṃ prāhur mūla-bandhaṃ hi yoginaḥ // HYP_3.62 //
children.translated_text: through this contraction, the <s>yogins</s> call it <s>Mūla bandha</s> (root lock). // HYP 3.62 //

children.text: gudaṃ pārṣṇyā tu sampīḍya vāyum ākuñcayed balāt /
children.translated_text: Pressing the anus with the heel, one should forcefully contract the breath,

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ yathā cordhvaṃ samāyāti samīraṇaḥ // HYP_3.63 //
children.translated_text: again and again, so that the air rises upward. // HYP 3.63 //

children.text: prāṇāpānau nāda-bindū mūla-bandhena caikatām /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, <s>nāda</s> (sound) and <s>bindu</s> (essence), through <s>Mūla bandha</s> attain unity;

children.text: gatvā yogasya saṃsiddhiṃ yacchato nātra saṃśayaḥ // HYP_3.64 //
children.translated_text: they bestow the perfection of <s>yoga</s> — there is no doubt in this. // HYP 3.64 //

children.text: apāna-prāṇayor aikyaṃ kṣayo mūtra-purīṣayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The union of <s>apāna</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>, the diminution of urine and feces,

children.text: yuvā bhavati vṛddho'pi satataṃ mūla-bandhanāt // HYP_3.65 //
children.translated_text: even an old person becomes young through constant practice of <s>Mūla bandha</s>. // HYP 3.65 //

children.text: apāna ūrdhvage jāte prayāte vahni-maṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: When <s>apāna</s> rises upward and reaches the sphere of fire,

children.text: tadānala-śikhā dīrghā jāyate vāyunāhatā // HYP_3.66 //
children.translated_text: then the flame of that fire becomes elongated, fanned by the wind. // HYP 3.66 //

children.text: tato yāto vahny-apānau prāṇam uṣṇa-svarūpakam /
children.translated_text: Then the fire and <s>apāna</s> reach <s>prāṇa</s>, which is hot by nature;

children.text: tenātyanta-pradīptas tu jvalano dehajas tathā // HYP_3.67 //
children.translated_text: thereby the bodily fire, extremely kindled, blazes forth. // HYP 3.67 //

children.text: tena kuṇḍalinī suptā santaptā samprabudhyate /
children.translated_text: Through that, the sleeping <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, being heated, is fully awakened;

children.text: daṇḍāhatā bhujaṅgīva niśvasya ṛjutāṃ vrajet // HYP_3.68 //
children.translated_text: like a serpent struck by a stick, she hisses and becomes straight. // HYP 3.68 //

children.text: bilaṃ praviṣṭeva tato brahma-nāḍyaṃ taraṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: Then, like (a serpent) entering its hole, she quickly enters the <s>Brahma-nāḍī</s> (suṣumnā);

children.text: tasmān nityaṃ mūla-bandhaḥ kartavyo yogibhiḥ sadā // HYP_3.69 //
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Mūla bandha</s> should always be constantly practiced by <s>yogins</s>. // HYP 3.69 //

children.text: atha jalandhara-bandhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Jālandhara Bandha</s> (the Net-Bearing Lock):

children.text: kaṇṭham ākuñcya hṛdaye sthāpayec cibukaṃ dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Contracting the throat, one should firmly place the chin on the chest;

children.text: bandho jālandharākhyo'yaṃ jarā-mṛtyu-vināśakaḥ // HYP_3.70 //
children.translated_text: this lock called <s>Jālandhara</s> destroys old age and death. // HYP 3.70 //

children.text: badhnāti hi sirājālam adho-gāmi nabho-jalam /
children.translated_text: It binds the network of channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>) through which the celestial water (<s>nabho-jala</s>) flows downward;

children.text: tato jālandharo bandhaḥ kaṇṭha-duḥkhaugha-nāśanaḥ // HYP_3.71 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is called <s>Jālandhara bandha</s> (net-lock), the destroyer of the flood of throat ailments. // HYP 3.71 //

children.text: jālandhare kṛte bandhe kaṇṭha-saṃkoca-lakṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: When <s>Jālandhara bandha</s> is performed, characterized by the contraction of the throat,

children.text: na pīyūṣaṃ pataty agnau na ca vāyuḥ prakupyati // HYP_3.72 //
children.translated_text: the nectar does not fall into the (digestive) fire, and the breath does not become agitated. // HYP 3.72 //

children.text: kaṇṭha-saṃkocanenaiva dve nāḍyau stambhayed dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Through the contraction of the throat alone, one should firmly stop the two <s>nāḍīs</s> (<s>iḍā</s> and <s>piṅgalā</s>);

children.text: madhya-cakram idaṃ jñeyaṃ ṣoḍaśādhāra-bandhanam // HYP_3.73 //
children.translated_text: this is known as the middle <s>cakra</s>, the binding of the sixteen supports. // HYP 3.73 //

children.text: mūla-sthānaṃ samākuñcya uḍḍiyānaṃ tu kārayet /
children.translated_text: Having contracted the root (<s>mūla</s>), one should perform <s>Uḍḍīyāna</s>;

children.text: iḍāṃ ca piṅgalāṃ baddhvā vāhayet paścime pathi // HYP_3.74 //
children.translated_text: having bound <s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>, one should make (the breath) flow in the posterior path. // HYP 3.74 //

children.text: anenaiva vidhānena prayāti pavano layam /
children.translated_text: By this very method, the breath attains dissolution (<s>laya</s>);

children.text: tato na jāyate mṛtyur jarā-rogādikaṃ tathā // HYP_3.75 //
children.translated_text: then death, old age, disease, and such do not occur. // HYP 3.75 //

children.text: bandha-trayam idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ mahā-siddhaiś ca sevitam /
children.translated_text: This triad of locks is the best, practiced by the great <s>siddhas</s>;

children.text: sarveṣāṃ haṭha-tantrāṇāṃ sādhanaṃ yogino viduḥ // HYP_3.76 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogins</s> know it as the means of all <s>haṭha-tantra</s> practices. // HYP 3.76 //

children.text: yat kiṃcit sravate candrād amṛtaṃ divya-rūpiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever nectar flows from the moon of divine form at the crown,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ grasate sūryas tena piṇḍo jarāyutaḥ // HYP_3.77 //
children.translated_text: all of it is consumed by the sun — hence the body becomes subject to old age. // HYP 3.77 //

children.text: atha viparīta-karaṇī mudrā-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Viparītakaraṇī Mudrā</s> (the Inverted Action Seal):

children.text: tatrāsti karaṇaṃ divyaṃ sūryasya mukha-vañcanam /
children.translated_text: There is a divine technique to deceive the mouth of the sun;

children.text: gurūpadeśato jñeyaṃ na tu śāstrārtha-koṭibhiḥ // HYP_3.78 //
children.translated_text: it should be known from the instruction of the <s>guru</s>, not from millions of scriptural interpretations. // HYP 3.78 //

children.text: ūrdhva-nābher adhas tālor ūrdhvaṃ bhānur adhaḥ śaśī /
children.translated_text: The sun is above the navel and below the palate; the moon is below (the palate) and above (the navel);

children.text: karaṇī viparītākhā guru-vākyena labhyate // HYP_3.79 //
children.translated_text: the technique called <s>Viparītā</s> (inverted) is obtained from the words of the <s>guru</s>. // HYP 3.79 //

children.text: nityam abhyāsa-yuktasya jaṭharāgni-vivardhanī /
children.translated_text: For one always engaged in practice, it increases the digestive fire;

children.text: āhāro bahulas tasya sampādyaḥ sādhakasya ca // HYP_3.80 //
children.translated_text: Abundant food should be procured by that practitioner // HYP 3.80 //

children.text: alpāhāro yadi bhaved agnir dahati tat-kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: If the food is insufficient, the fire will burn [the body] immediately;

children.text: adhaḥ-śirāś cordhva-pādaḥ kṣaṇaṃ syāt prathame dine // HYP_3.81 //
children.translated_text: On the first day, one should remain head-down and feet-up for a moment // HYP 3.81 //

children.text: kṣaṇāc ca kiṃcid adhikam abhyasec ca dine dine /
children.translated_text: And one should practice a little more than a moment, day by day;

children.text: valitaṃ palitaṃ caiva ṣaṇmāsordhvaṃ na dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Wrinkles and grey hair indeed are not seen after six months;

children.text: yāma-mātraṃ tu yo nityam abhyaset sa tu kālajit // HYP_3.82 //
children.translated_text: One who daily practices for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) is indeed a conqueror of time // HYP 3.82 //

children.text: atha vajrolī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Vajrolī</s> —

children.text: svecchayā vartamāno'pi yogoktair niyamair vinā /
children.translated_text: Even living by one's own will, without the restraints prescribed by yoga,

children.text: vajrolīṃ yo vijānāti sa yogī siddhi-bhājanam // HYP_3.83 //
children.translated_text: One who knows <s>Vajrolī</s> — that <s>yogin</s> is a vessel of attainment // HYP 3.83 //

children.text: tatra vastu-dvayaṃ vakṣye durlabhaṃ yasya kasyacit /
children.translated_text: In that [practice], I shall describe two things, difficult to obtain for anyone;

children.text: kṣīraṃ caikaṃ dvitīyaṃ tu nārī ca vaśa-vartinī // HYP_3.84 //
children.translated_text: One is milk, and the second is a woman who is compliant // HYP 3.84 //

children.text: mehanena śanaiḥ samyag ūrdhvākuñcanam abhyaset /
children.translated_text: Through the male organ, one should slowly and properly practice the upward contraction;

children.text: puruṣo'py athavā nārī vajrolī-siddhim āpnuyāt // HYP_3.85 //
children.translated_text: Whether man or woman, one may attain the perfection of <s>Vajrolī</s> // HYP 3.85 //

children.text: yatnataḥ śasta-nālena phūtkāraṃ vajra-kandare /
children.translated_text: With effort, through an instrument-tube, blowing into the <s>vajra</s>-canal,

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiḥ prakurvīta vāyu-saṃcāra-kāraṇāt // HYP_3.86 //
children.translated_text: One should practice slowly and gradually, for the purpose of circulating air // HYP 3.86 //

children.text: nārī-bhage padad-bindum abhyāsenordhvam āharet /
children.translated_text: Through practice, one should draw upward the <s>bindu</s> that has fallen into the woman's womb;

children.text: calitaṃ ca nijaṃ bindum ūrdhvam ākṛṣya rakṣayet // HYP_3.87 //
children.translated_text: And having drawn one's own displaced <s>bindu</s> upward, one should preserve it // HYP 3.87 //

children.text: evaṃ saṃrakṣayed binduṃ jayati yogavit /
children.translated_text: Thus, by preserving the <s>bindu</s>, the knower of yoga conquers [death];

children.text: maraṇaṃ bindu-pātena jīvanaṃ bindu-dhāraṇāt // HYP_3.88 //
children.translated_text: Death [comes] from the falling of the <s>bindu</s>, life from the retention of the <s>bindu</s> // HYP 3.88 //

children.text: sugandho yogino dehe jāyate bindu-dhāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: A pleasant fragrance arises in the body of the <s>yogin</s> from the retention of the <s>bindu</s>;

children.text: yāvad binduḥ sthiro dehe tāvat kāla-bhayaṃ kutaḥ // HYP_3.89 //
children.translated_text: As long as the <s>bindu</s> is steady in the body, whence the fear of death? // HYP 3.89 //

children.text: cittāyattaṃ nṝṇāṃ śukraṃ śukrāyattaṃ ca jīvitam /
children.translated_text: The semen of men depends on the mind, and life depends on the semen;

children.text: tasmāc chukraṃ manaś caiva rakṣaṇīyaṃ prayatnataḥ // HYP_3.90 //
children.translated_text: Therefore both semen and mind should be preserved with effort // HYP 3.90 //

children.text: ṛtumatyā rajo'py evaṃ nijaṃ binduṃ ca rakṣayet /
children.translated_text: A menstruating woman should likewise preserve her own <s>rajas</s> and <s>bindu</s>;

children.text: meḍhreṇākarṣayed ūrdhvaṃ samyag abhyāsa-yoga-vit // HYP_3.91 //
children.translated_text: One skilled in the practice of yoga should draw it upward through the organ // HYP 3.91 //

children.text: atha sahajoliḥ-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Sahajolī</s> —

children.text: sahajoliś cāmarolir vajrolyā bheda ekataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sahajolī</s> and <s>Amarolī</s> are varieties of <s>Vajrolī</s>;

children.text: jale subhasma nikṣipya dagdha-gomaya-sambhavam // HYP_3.92 //
children.translated_text: Sprinkling in water sacred ash produced from burnt cow dung // HYP 3.92 //

children.text: vajrolī-maithunād ūrdhvaṃ strī-puṃsoḥ svāṅga-lepanam /
children.translated_text: After the intercourse of <s>Vajrolī</s>, the anointing of one's own limbs by both man and woman,

children.text: āsīnayoḥ sukhenaiva mukta-vyāpārayoḥ kṣaṇāt // HYP_3.93 //
children.translated_text: While sitting comfortably, free from activity, after a moment // HYP 3.93 //

children.text: sahajolir iyaṃ proktā śraddheyā yogibhiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: This is declared as <s>Sahajolī</s>, to be always trusted by <s>yogins</s>;

children.text: ayaṃ śubha-karo yogo bhoga-yukto'pi muktidaḥ // HYP_3.94 //
children.translated_text: This yoga is auspicious and grants liberation even when conjoined with enjoyment // HYP 3.94 //

children.text: ayaṃ yogaḥ puṇyavatāṃ dhīrāṇāṃ tattva-darśinām /
children.translated_text: This yoga succeeds for the meritorious, the brave, and the seers of truth;

children.text: nirmatsarāṇāṃ vai sidhyen na tu matsara-śālinām // HYP_3.95 //
children.translated_text: It succeeds for those free from envy, but not for the envious // HYP 3.95 //

children.text: pittolbaṇatvāt prathamāmbu-dhārāṃ
children.translated_text: Discarding the first stream of water due to excess of <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: vihāya niḥsāratayānty adhārām /
children.translated_text: And [discarding] the last stream as without essence,

children.text: niṣevyate śītala-madhya-dhārā
children.translated_text: One should consume the cool middle stream;

children.text: kāpālike khaṇḍamate'marolī // HYP_3.96 //
children.translated_text: This is <s>Amarolī</s> according to the <s>Kāpālika</s> <s>Khaṇḍamata</s> (doctrine) // HYP 3.96 //

children.text: amarīṃ yaḥ piben nityaṃ nasyaṃ kurvan dine dine /
children.translated_text: One who daily drinks <s>amarī</s>, practicing nasal application day by day,

children.text: vajrolīm abhyaset samyak sāmarolīti kathyate // HYP_3.97 //
children.translated_text: And properly practices <s>Vajrolī</s> — that is called <s>Sāmarolī</s> // HYP 3.97 //

children.text: abhyāsān niḥsṛtāṃ cāndrīṃ vibhūtyā saha miśrayet /
children.translated_text: The lunar [essence] that flows out from practice, one should mix with sacred ash;

children.text: dhārayed uttamāṅgeṣu divya-dṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate // HYP_3.98 //
children.translated_text: Applied on the upper parts of the body, divine vision arises // HYP 3.98 //

children.text: puṃso binduṃ samākuñcya samyag abhyāsa-pāṭavāt /
children.translated_text: Having contracted the <s>bindu</s> of the man through the skill of proper practice,

children.text: yadi nārī rajo rakṣed vajrolyā sāpi yoginī // HYP_3.99 //
children.translated_text: If a woman preserves her <s>rajas</s> through <s>Vajrolī</s>, she too is a <s>yoginī</s> // HYP 3.99 //

children.text: tasyāḥ kiṃcid rajo nāśaṃ na gacchati na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not even a little of her <s>rajas</s> is lost, without doubt;

children.text: tasyāḥ śarīre nādaś ca bindutām eva gacchati // HYP_3.100 //
children.translated_text: And in her body, the <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) attains the state of <s>bindu</s> // HYP 3.100 //

children.text: sa bindus tad rajaś caiva ekībhūya svadehagau /
children.translated_text: That <s>bindu</s> and that <s>rajas</s>, having become one within one's own body,

children.text: vajroly-abhyāsa-yogena sarva-siddhiṃ prayacchataḥ // HYP_3.101 //
children.translated_text: Through the yoga of <s>Vajrolī</s> practice, grant all <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) // HYP 3.101 //

children.text: rakṣed ākuñcanād ūrdhvaṃ yā rajaḥ sā hi yoginī /
children.translated_text: She who preserves her <s>rajas</s> by drawing it upward through contraction is indeed a <s>yoginī</s>;

children.text: atītānāgataṃ vetti khecarī ca bhaved dhruvam // HYP_3.102 //
children.translated_text: She knows the past and future, and certainly attains <s>khecarī</s> // HYP 3.102 //

children.text: deha-siddhiṃ ca labhate vajroly-abhyāsa-yogataḥ /
children.translated_text: One obtains perfection of the body through the yoga of <s>Vajrolī</s> practice;

children.text: ayaṃ puṇya-karo yogo bhoge bhukte'pi muktidaḥ // HYP_3.103 //
children.translated_text: This yoga bestows merit and grants liberation even while enjoying pleasures // HYP 3.103 //

children.text: atha śakti-cālanam-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Śakticālana</s> (stirring of the power) —

children.text: kuṭilāṅgī kuṇḍalinī bhujaṅgī śaktir īśvarī /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṭilāṅgī</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, <s>Bhujaṅgī</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Īśvarī</s>,

children.text: kuṇḍaly arundhatī caite śabdāḥ paryāya-vācakāḥ // HYP_3.104 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>, <s>Arundhatī</s> — these are synonymous terms // HYP 3.104 //

children.text: udghāṭayet kapāṭaṃ tu yathā kuṃcikayā haṭhāt /
children.translated_text: Just as one opens a door by force with a key,

children.text: kuṇḍalinyā tathā yogī mokṣadvāraṃ vibhedayet // HYP_3.105 //
children.translated_text: So the <s>yogin</s> should break open the door to liberation through <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> // HYP 3.105 //

children.text: yena mārgeṇa gantavyaṃ brahma-sthānaṃ nirāmayam /
children.translated_text: By which path one must travel to the painless abode of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: mukhenācchādya tad vāraṃ prasuptā parameśvarī // HYP_3.106 //
children.translated_text: Covering that entrance with her mouth, the supreme Goddess (<s>Parameśvarī</s>) sleeps // HYP 3.106 //

children.text: kandordhve kuṇḍalī śaktiḥ suptā mokṣāya yoginām /
children.translated_text: Above the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), the <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> power lies asleep — for liberation of <s>yogins</s>;

children.text: bandhanāya ca mūḍhānāṃ yas tāṃ vetti sa yogavit // HYP_3.107 //
children.translated_text: And for bondage of the deluded — one who knows her is a knower of yoga // HYP 3.107 //

children.text: kuṇḍalī kuṭilākārā sarpavat parikīrtitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> is described as having a coiled form, like a serpent;

children.text: sā śaktiś cālitā yena sa mukto nātra saṃśayaḥ // HYP_3.108 //
children.translated_text: One by whom that power is stirred is liberated — there is no doubt in this // HYP 3.108 //

children.text: gaṅgā-yamunayor madhye bāla-raṇḍāṃ tapasvinīm /
children.translated_text: Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, the young widow ascetic,

children.text: balātkāreṇa gṛhṇīyāt tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // HYP_3.109 //
children.translated_text: One should seize by force — that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> // HYP 3.109 //

children.text: iḍā bhagavatī gaṅgā piṅgalā yamunā nadī /
children.translated_text: <s>Iḍā</s> is the blessed <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s> is the river <s>Yamunā</s>;

children.text: iḍā-piṅgalayor madhye bālaraṇḍā ca kuṇḍalī // HYP_3.110 //
children.translated_text: Between <s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>, the young widow is <s>Kuṇḍalī</s> // HYP 3.110 //

children.text: pucche pragṛhya bhujaṅgīṃ suptām udbodhayec ca tām /
children.translated_text: Grasping the sleeping serpent (<s>Bhujaṅgī</s>) by its tail, one should awaken it;

children.text: nidrāṃ vihāya sā śaktir ūrdhvam uttiṣṭhate haṭhāt // HYP_3.111 //
children.translated_text: Abandoning sleep, that power rises upward by force // HYP 3.111 //

children.text: avasthitā caiva phaṇāvatī sā
children.translated_text: And she remains, that hooded one,

children.text: prātaś ca sāyaṃ praharārdha-mātram /
children.translated_text: In the morning and evening, for half a <s>prahara</s> (one and a half hours);

children.text: prapūrya sūryāt paridhāna-yuktyā
children.translated_text: Filling from the <s>sūrya</s> (right nostril) with the technique of holding,

children.text: pragṛhya nityaṃ paricālanīyā // HYP_3.112 //
children.translated_text: Having grasped [her], she should be constantly moved about // HYP 3.112 //

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ vitasti-mātraṃ tu vistāraṃ caturaṅgulam /
children.translated_text: Upward, the span of one <s>vitasti</s> (twelve finger-breadths), with a width of four finger-breadths,

children.text: mṛdulaṃ dhavalaṃ proktaṃ veṣṭitāmbara-lakṣaṇam // HYP_3.113 //
children.translated_text: Soft, white, and described as having the appearance of a wrapped cloth // HYP 3.113 //

children.text: sati vajrāsane pādau karābhyāṃ dhārayed dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Being in <s>Vajrāsana</s>, one should firmly hold the feet with both hands;

children.text: gulpha-deśa-samīpe ca kandaṃ tatra prapīḍayet // HYP_3.114 //
children.translated_text: And near the ankle region, one should press the <s>kanda</s> (bulb) there // HYP 3.114 //

children.text: vajrāsane sthito yogī cālayitvā ca kuṇḍalīm /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s>, seated in <s>Vajrāsana</s>, having stirred the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>,

children.text: kuryād anantaraṃ bhastrāṃ kuṇḍalīm āśu bodhayet // HYP_3.115 //
children.translated_text: Should then perform <s>Bhastrā</s> (bellows breath) to quickly awaken the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> // HYP 3.115 //

children.text: bhānor ākuñcanaṃ kuryāt kuṇḍalīṃ cālayet tataḥ /
children.translated_text: One should contract the <s>sūrya</s> (solar plexus) and thereby stir the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>;

children.text: mṛtyu-vaktra-gatasyāpi tasya mṛtyu-bhayaṃ kutaḥ // HYP_3.116 //
children.translated_text: Even for one who has entered the mouth of death, whence the fear of death? // HYP 3.116 //

children.text: muhūrta-dvaya-paryantaṃ nirbhayaṃ cālanād asau /
children.translated_text: Through fearless stirring for the duration of two <s>muhūrtas</s> (ninety-six minutes),

children.text: ūrdhvam ākṛṣyate kiṃcit suṣumṇāyāṃ samudgatā // HYP_3.117 //
children.translated_text: [The <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>] is drawn upward somewhat, having risen into the <s>Suṣumnā</s> // HYP 3.117 //

children.text: tena kuṇḍalinī tasyāḥ suṣumṇāyā mukhaṃ dhruvam /
children.translated_text: By this, the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> certainly [enters] the mouth of the <s>Suṣumnā</s>;

children.text: jahāti tasmāt prāṇo'yaṃ suṣumṇāṃ vrajati svataḥ // HYP_3.118 //
children.translated_text: Therefore this <s>prāṇa</s> enters the <s>Suṣumnā</s> of its own accord // HYP 3.118 //

children.text: tasmāt saṃcālayen nityaṃ sukha-suptām arundhatīm /
children.translated_text: Therefore one should daily stir <s>Arundhatī</s> (<s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>) who sleeps comfortably;

children.text: tasyāḥ saṃcālanenaiva yogī rogaiḥ pramucyate // HYP_3.119 //
children.translated_text: By her stirring alone, the <s>yogin</s> is freed from diseases // HYP 3.119 //

children.text: yena saṃcālitā śaktiḥ sa yogī siddhi-bhājanam /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> by whom the power is stirred is a vessel of attainment;

children.text: kim atra bahunoktena kālaṃ jayati līlayā // HYP_3.120 //
children.translated_text: What need is there of saying more? He conquers time effortlessly // HYP 3.120 //

children.text: brahmacarya-ratasyaiva nityaṃ hita-mitāśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one devoted to <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), always eating beneficial and measured food,

children.text: maṇḍalād dṛśyate siddhiḥ kuṇḍaly-abhyāsa-yoginaḥ // HYP_3.121 //
children.translated_text: Attainment is seen within a <s>maṇḍala</s> (forty days) for the practitioner of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> yoga // HYP 3.121 //

children.text: kuṇḍalīṃ cālayitvā tu bhastrāṃ kuryād viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having stirred the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, one should especially perform <s>Bhastrā</s> (bellows breath);

children.text: evam abhyasyato nityaṃ yamino yama-bhīḥ kutaḥ // HYP_3.122 //
children.translated_text: For one who practices thus daily with self-restraint, whence the fear of <s>Yama</s> (death)? // HYP 3.122 //

children.text: dvā-saptati-sahasrāṇāṃ nāḍīnāṃ mala-śodhane /
children.translated_text: For purifying the impurities of seventy-two thousand <s>nāḍīs</s>,

children.text: kutaḥ prakṣālanopāyaḥ kuṇḍaly-abhyasanād ṛte // HYP_3.123 //
children.translated_text: What means of cleansing is there other than the practice of <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>? // HYP 3.123 //

children.text: iyaṃ tu madhyamā nāḍī dṛḍhābhyāsena yoginām /
children.translated_text: But this central channel (<s>madhyamā nāḍī</s>), through firm practice by <s>yogins</s>,

children.text: āsana-prāṇa-saṃyāma-mudrābhiḥ saralā bhavet // HYP_3.124 //
children.translated_text: Becomes straight through <s>āsanas</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and <s>mudrās</s> // HYP 3.124 //

children.text: abhyāse tu vinidrāṇāṃ mano dhṛtvā samādhinā /
children.translated_text: In the practice of those who are free from drowsiness, having held the mind in <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: rudrāṇī vā parā mudrā bhadrāṃ siddhiṃ prayacchati // HYP_3.125 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rudrāṇī</s> or <s>Parā Mudrā</s> grants auspicious attainment // HYP 3.125 //

children.text: rāja-yogaṃ vinā pṛthvī rāja-yogaṃ vinā niśā /
children.translated_text: Without <s>Rājayoga</s>, the earth [is incomplete]; without <s>Rājayoga</s>, the night [is incomplete];

children.text: rāja-yogaṃ vinā mudrā vicitrāpi na śobhate // HYP_3.126 //
children.translated_text: Without <s>Rājayoga</s>, even a wondrous <s>mudrā</s> does not shine // HYP 3.126 //

children.text: mārutasya vidhiṃ sarvaṃ mano-yuktaṃ samabhyaset /
children.translated_text: All the procedures of breath should be practiced with the mind engaged;

children.text: itaratra na kartavyā mano-vṛttir manīṣiṇā // HYP_3.127 //
children.translated_text: The wise one should not direct the mental activity elsewhere // HYP 3.127 //

children.text: iti mudrā daśa proktā ādināthena śambhunā /
children.translated_text: Thus ten <s>mudrās</s> have been declared by <s>Ādinātha</s> <s>Śambhu</s>;

children.text: ekaikā tāsu yamināṃ mahā-siddhi-pradāyinī // HYP_3.128 //
children.translated_text: Each one of them bestows great <s>siddhis</s> upon the self-controlled // HYP 3.128 //

children.text: upadeśaṃ hi mudrāṇāṃ yo datte sāmpradāyikam /
children.translated_text: He who gives the traditional instruction of the <s>mudrās</s>,

children.text: sa eva śrī-guruḥ svāmī sākṣād īśvara eva saḥ // HYP_3.129 //
children.translated_text: He alone is the blessed <s>guru</s>, the master — he is verily <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) himself // HYP 3.129 //

children.text: tasya vākya-paro bhūtvā mudrābhyāse samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having become devoted to his words, absorbed in the practice of <s>mudrās</s>,

children.text: aṇimādi-guṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ labhate kāla-vañcanam // HYP_3.130 //
children.translated_text: One attains the deception of death along with the powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) // HYP 3.130 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the <s>Haṭhapradīpikā</s>.

children.text: namaḥ śivāya gurave nāda-bindu-kalātmane /
children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Śiva</s>, the <s>guru</s>, whose nature is <s>nāda</s>, <s>bindu</s>, and <s>kalā</s>;

children.text: nirañjana-padaṃ yāti nityaṃ tatra parāyaṇaḥ // HYP_4.1 //
children.translated_text: One who is always devoted to that attains the stainless state // HYP 4.1 //

children.text: athedānīṃ pravakṣyāmi samādhikramam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the supreme process of <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: mṛtyughnaṃ ca sukhopāyaṃ brahmānanda-karaṃ param // HYP_4.2 //
children.translated_text: Which destroys death, is an easy means, and produces the supreme bliss of <s>Brahman</s> // HYP 4.2 //

children.text: rāja-yogaḥ samādhiś ca unmanī ca manonmanī /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājayoga</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, <s>unmanī</s>, <s>manonmanī</s>,

children.text: amaratvaṃ layas tattvaṃ śūnyāśūnyaṃ paraṃ padam // HYP_4.3 //
children.translated_text: Immortality, <s>laya</s> (dissolution), <s>tattva</s> (reality), <s>śūnyāśūnya</s> (void and non-void), <s>paraṃ padam</s> (supreme state), // HYP 4.3 //

children.text: amanaskaṃ tathādvaitaṃ nirālambaṃ nirañjanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Amanaska</s> (mindless), <s>advaita</s> (non-dual), <s>nirālamba</s> (without support), <s>nirañjana</s> (stainless),

children.text: jīvanmuktiś ca sahajā turyā cety eka-vācakāḥ // HYP_4.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), <s>sahajā</s> (innate), <s>turyā</s> (the fourth) — these are synonymous terms // HYP 4.4 //

children.text: salile saindhavaṃ yadvat sāmyaṃ bhajati yogataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as salt becomes unified with water through union,

children.text: tathātma-manasor aikyaṃ samādhir abhidhīyate // HYP_4.5 //
children.translated_text: So the unity of Self and mind is called <s>samādhi</s> // HYP 4.5 //

children.text: yadā saṃkṣīyate prāṇo mānasaṃ ca pralīyate /
children.translated_text: When <s>prāṇa</s> diminishes and the mind dissolves,

children.text: tadā samarasatvaṃ ca samādhir abhidhīyate // HYP_4.6 //
children.translated_text: Then the state of equal essence (<s>samarasatva</s>) is called <s>samādhi</s> // HYP 4.6 //

children.text: tat-samaṃ ca dvayor aikyaṃ jīvātma-paramātmanoḥ /
children.translated_text: That equality, the unity of the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) and the supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>),

children.text: pranaṣṭa-sarva-saṅkalpaḥ samādhiḥ so'bhidhīyate // HYP_4.7 //
children.translated_text: [When] all thought-constructs are destroyed — that is called <s>samādhi</s> // HYP 4.7 //

children.text: rāja-yogasya māhātmyaṃ ko vā jānāti tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Who indeed knows the greatness of <s>Rājayoga</s> in truth?

children.text: jñānaṃ muktiḥ sthitiḥ siddhir guru-vākyena labhyate // HYP_4.8 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge, liberation, steadiness, and attainment are obtained through the word of the <s>guru</s> // HYP 4.8 //

children.text: durlabho viṣaya-tyāgo durlabhaṃ tattva-darśanam /
children.translated_text: Difficult is the renunciation of sense-objects, difficult is the vision of truth,

children.text: durlabhā sahajāvasthā sad-guroḥ karuṇāṃ vinā // HYP_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Difficult is the natural state (<s>sahajāvasthā</s>) without the compassion of the true <s>guru</s> // HYP 4.9 //

children.text: vividhair āsanaiḥ kubhair vicitraiḥ karaṇair api /
children.translated_text: Through various <s>āsanas</s>, <s>kumbhakas</s> (breath retentions), and diverse practices,

children.text: prabuddhāyāṃ mahā-śaktau prāṇaḥ śūnye pralīyate // HYP_4.10 //
children.translated_text: When the great power is awakened, <s>prāṇa</s> dissolves in the void (<s>śūnya</s>) // HYP 4.10 //

children.text: utpanna-śakti-bodhasya tyakta-niḥśeṣa-karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one in whom the awakening of the power has arisen, who has abandoned all <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: yoginaḥ sahajāvasthā svayam eva prajāyate // HYP_4.11 //
children.translated_text: The natural state (<s>sahajāvasthā</s>) of the <s>yogin</s> arises of its own accord // HYP 4.11 //

children.text: suṣumṇā-vāhini prāṇe śūnye viśati mānase /
children.translated_text: When <s>prāṇa</s> flows in the <s>Suṣumnā</s> and the mind enters the void,

children.text: tadā sarvāṇi karmāṇi nirmūlayati yogavit // HYP_4.12 //
children.translated_text: Then the knower of yoga uproots all <s>karmas</s> // HYP 4.12 //

children.text: amarāya namas tubhyaṃ so'pi kālas tvayā jitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutations to you, O immortal one! Even time has been conquered by you,

children.text: patitaṃ vadane yasya jagad etac carācaram // HYP_4.13 //
children.translated_text: In whose mouth this entire world, moving and unmoving, has fallen // HYP 4.13 //

children.text: citte samatvam āpanne vāyau vrajati madhyame /
children.translated_text: When the mind attains equanimity and the breath enters the middle [channel],

children.text: tadāmarolī vajrolī sahajolī prajāyate // HYP_4.14 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Amarolī</s>, <s>Vajrolī</s>, and <s>Sahajolī</s> are [naturally] accomplished // HYP 4.14 //

children.text: jñānaṃ kuto manasi sambhavatīha tāvat
children.translated_text: How can knowledge arise in the mind as long as

children.text: prāṇo'pi jīvati mano mriyate na yāvat /
children.translated_text: The breath also lives and the mind does not die?

children.text: prāṇo mano dvayam idaṃ vilayaṃ nayed yo
children.translated_text: One who leads these two — breath and mind — to dissolution,

children.text: mokṣaṃ sa gacchati naro na kathaṃcid anyaḥ // HYP_4.15 //
children.translated_text: That person attains liberation — no one else by any means // HYP 4.15 //

children.text: jñātvā suṣumṇāsad-bhedaṃ kṛtvā vāyuṃ ca madhyagam /
children.translated_text: Having known the opening of the <s>Suṣumnā</s> and having made the breath enter the middle,

children.text: sthitvā sadaiva susthāne brahma-randhre nirodhayet // HYP_4.16 //
children.translated_text: Remaining always in the proper place, one should restrain [it] at the <s>brahmarandhra</s> // HYP 4.16 //

children.text: sūrya-candramasau dhattaḥ kālaṃ rātrindivātmakam /
children.translated_text: The sun and moon create time consisting of day and night;

children.text: bhoktrī suṣumnā kālasya guhyam etad udāhṛtam // HYP_4.17 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Suṣumnā</s> is the consumer of time — this secret has been declared // HYP 4.17 //

children.text: dvā-saptati-sahasrāṇi nāḍī-dvārāṇi pañjare /
children.translated_text: There are seventy-two thousand channel-openings in the body;

children.text: suṣumṇā śāmbhavī śaktiḥ śeṣās tv eva nirarthakāḥ // HYP_4.18 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Suṣumnā</s> is the <s>Śāmbhavī Śakti</s>; the rest are truly purposeless // HYP 4.18 //

children.text: vāyuḥ paricito yasmād agninā saha kuṇḍalīm /
children.translated_text: Since the breath, together with fire, having aroused the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>,

children.text: bodhayitvā suṣumṇāyāṃ praviśed anirodhataḥ // HYP_4.19 //
children.translated_text: After awakening it, should enter the <s>Suṣumnā</s> without obstruction // HYP 4.19 //

children.text: suṣumṇā-vāhini prāṇe siddhyaty eva manonmanī /
children.translated_text: When <s>prāṇa</s> flows in the <s>Suṣumnā</s>, <s>manonmanī</s> (the state beyond mind) is indeed attained;

children.text: anyathā tv itarābhyāsāḥ prayāsāyaiva yoginām // HYP_4.20 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, all other practices are mere exertion for <s>yogins</s> // HYP 4.20 //

children.text: pavano badhyate yena manas tenaiva badhyate /
children.translated_text: That by which breath is restrained — by that very [means] the mind is restrained;

children.text: manaś ca badhyate yena pavanas tena badhyate // HYP_4.21 //
children.translated_text: And that by which the mind is restrained — by that breath is restrained // HYP 4.21 //

children.text: hetu-dvayaṃ tu cittasya vāsanā ca samīraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The two causes of the mind are <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) and breath;

children.text: tayor vinaṣṭa ekasmin tau dvāv api vinaśyataḥ // HYP_4.22 //
children.translated_text: When one of those two is destroyed, both are destroyed // HYP 4.22 //

children.text: mano yatra vilīyeta pavanas tatra līyate /
children.translated_text: Where the mind dissolves, there the breath dissolves;

children.text: pavano līyate yatra manas tatra vilīyate // HYP_4.23 //
children.translated_text: Where the breath dissolves, there the mind dissolves // HYP 4.23 //

children.text: dugdhāmbuvat saṃmilitāv ubhau tau
children.translated_text: Like milk and water, those two are mixed together,

children.text: tulya-kriyau mānasa-mārutau hi /
children.translated_text: Indeed, the mind and breath have equal activity;

children.text: yato marut tatra manaḥ-pravṛttir
children.translated_text: Where breath [moves], there is the activity of the mind;

children.text: yato manas tatra marut-pravṛttiḥ // HYP_4.24 //
children.translated_text: Where the mind [moves], there is the activity of breath // HYP 4.24 //

children.text: tatraika-nāśād aparasya nāśa
children.translated_text: By the destruction of one of them, the other is destroyed;

children.text: eka-pravṛtter apara-pravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: From the activity of one arises the activity of the other;

children.text: adhvas tayoś cendriya-varga-vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: When these two remain, the activity of the group of senses [continues];

children.text: pradhvas tayor mokṣa-padasya siddhiḥ // HYP_4.25 //
children.translated_text: When these two are destroyed, the attainment of the state of liberation [occurs] // HYP 4.25 //

children.text: rasasya manasaś caiva cañcalatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury and the mind are by nature restless;

children.text: raso baddho mano baddhaṃ kiṃ na siddhyati bhūtale // HYP_4.26 //
children.translated_text: When mercury is bound and the mind is bound, what cannot be accomplished on earth? // HYP 4.26 //

children.text: mūrcchito harate vyādhīn mṛto jīvayati svayam /
children.translated_text: When stupefied, [mercury] removes diseases; when killed (fixed), it revives [the dead] itself;

children.text: baddhaḥ khecaratāṃ dhatte raso vāyuś ca pārvati // HYP_4.27 //
children.translated_text: When bound, both mercury and breath bestow the power of moving through space, O <s>Pārvatī</s> // HYP 4.27 //

children.text: manaḥ sthairyaṃ sthiro vāyus tato binduḥ sthiro bhavet /
children.translated_text: When the mind is steady, the breath is steady; from that, the <s>bindu</s> becomes steady;

children.text: bindu-sthairyāt sadā sattvaṃ piṇḍa-sthairyaṃ prajāyate // HYP_4.28 //
children.translated_text: From the steadiness of the <s>bindu</s>, there is always <s>sattva</s> (purity) — bodily steadiness arises // HYP 4.28 //

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ mano nātho manonāthas tu mārutaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind is the lord of the senses; the lord of the mind is breath;

children.text: mārutasya layo nāthaḥ sa layo nādam āśritaḥ // HYP_4.29 //
children.translated_text: The lord of breath is <s>laya</s> (dissolution); that <s>laya</s> depends on <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) // HYP 4.29 //

children.text: so'yam evāstu mokṣākhyo māstu vāpi matāntare /
children.translated_text: Let this very [state] be called liberation, or let it not [be so called] in another school of thought;

children.text: manaḥ-prāṇa-laye kaścid ānandaḥ sampravartate // HYP_4.30 //
children.translated_text: upon the dissolution of mind and breath, a certain bliss arises. (HYP 4.30)

children.text: pranaṣṭa-śvāsa-niśvāsaḥ pradhvasta-viṣaya-grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: With breath and exhalation ceased, with the grasp of sense-objects destroyed,

children.text: niśceṣṭo nirvikāraś ca layo jayati yoginām // HYP_4.31 //
children.translated_text: motionless and without modification — <s>laya</s> (dissolution) triumphs for the <s>yogīs</s>. (HYP 4.31)

children.text: ucchinna-sarva-saṅkalpo niḥśeṣāśeṣa-ceṣṭitaḥ /
children.translated_text: With all mental constructs cut off, with all activities completely ceased,

children.text: svāvagamyo layaḥ ko'pi jāyate vāg-agocaraḥ // HYP_4.32 //
children.translated_text: a certain <s>laya</s> arises, knowable only by oneself, beyond the reach of speech. (HYP 4.32)

children.text: yatra dṛṣṭir layas tatra bhūtendriya-sanātanī /
children.translated_text: Where the gaze [is fixed], there <s>laya</s> [occurs] — the eternal [power] of the elements and senses,

children.text: sā śaktir jīva-bhūtānāṃ dve alakṣye layaṃ gate // HYP_4.33 //
children.translated_text: that <s>śakti</s> (power), the life-essence of beings — both [mind and śakti], having entered the imperceptible, are dissolved. (HYP 4.33)

children.text: layo laya iti prāhuḥ kīdṛśaṃ laya-lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Laya</s>, <s>laya</s>' — thus they speak; what is the characteristic of <s>laya</s>?

children.text: apunar-vāsanotthānāl layo viṣaya-vismṛtiḥ // HYP_4.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Laya</s> is the forgetting of sense-objects, due to the non-arising of latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>). (HYP 4.34)

children.text: veda-śāstra-purāṇāni sāmānya-gaṇikā iva /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s>, scriptures, and <s>Purāṇas</s> are like common courtesans,

children.text: ekaiva śāmbhavī mudrā guptā kula-vadhūr iva // HYP_4.35 //
children.translated_text: but <s>Śāmbhavī Mudrā</s> alone is like a hidden noble wife. (HYP 4.35)

children.text: atha śāmbhavī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Śāmbhavī</s> [Mudrā]:

children.text: antar lakṣyaṃ bahir dṛṣṭir nimeṣonmeṣa-varjitā /
children.translated_text: The gaze directed outward while the focus is within, without blinking or closing the eyes —

children.text: eṣā sā śāmbhavī mudrā veda-śāstreṣu gopitā // HYP_4.36 //
children.translated_text: this is the <s>Śāmbhavī Mudrā</s>, concealed in the <s>Vedas</s> and scriptures. (HYP 4.36)

children.text: antar lakṣya-vilīna-citta-pavano yogī yadā vartate
children.translated_text: When the <s>yogī</s> abides with mind and breath dissolved in the inner focus,

children.text: dṛṣṭyā niścala-tārayā bahir adhaḥ paśyann apaśyann api /
children.translated_text: with steady, unmoving pupils, looking outward and downward, yet not really seeing,

children.text: mudreyaṃ khalu śāmbhavī bhavati sā labdhā prasādād guroḥ
children.translated_text: this is indeed <s>Śāmbhavī Mudrā</s>, obtained by the grace of the <s>guru</s> —

children.text: śūnyāśūnya-vilakṣaṇaṃ sphurati tat tattvaṃ padaṃ śāmbhavam // HYP_4.37 //
children.translated_text: that <s>tattva</s> (reality), the state of <s>Śambhu</s>, distinct from both void and non-void, shines forth. (HYP 4.37)

children.text: śrī-śāmbhavyāś ca khecaryā avasthā-dhāma-bhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the different states and stages of the revered <s>Śāmbhavī</s> and <s>Khecarī</s>,

children.text: bhavec citta-layānandaḥ śūnye cit-sukha-rūpiṇi // HYP_4.38 //
children.translated_text: the bliss of <s>citta-laya</s> (dissolution of mind) arises in the void that is of the nature of consciousness-bliss. (HYP 4.38)

children.text: tāre jyotiṣi saṃyojya kiṃcid unnamayed bhruvau /
children.translated_text: Joining the pupils to the inner light, one should slightly raise the eyebrows,

children.text: pūrva-yogaṃ mano yuñjann unmanī-kārakaḥ kṣaṇāt // HYP_4.39 //
children.translated_text: applying the previously described <s>yoga</s> to the mind — it produces <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind) in an instant. (HYP 4.39)

children.text: kecid āgama-jālena kecin nigama-saṅkulaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some are deluded by the web of scriptures, some by the mass of <s>Vedic</s> [texts],

children.text: kecit tarkeṇa muhyanti naiva jānanti tārakam // HYP_4.40 //
children.translated_text: some by logic — they do not know <s>Tāraka</s> (the liberating [reality]). (HYP 4.40)

children.text: ardhonmīlita-locanaḥ sthira-manā nāsāgra-dattekṣaṇaś
children.translated_text: With half-open eyes, steady mind, gaze fixed on the tip of the nose,

children.text: candrārkāv api līnatām upanayan nispanda-bhāvena yaḥ /
children.translated_text: dissolving both sun and moon [channels] with a motionless state,

children.text: jyotī-rūpam aśeṣa-bījam akhilaṃ dedīpyamānaṃ paraṃ
children.translated_text: the luminous form, the complete seed of all, blazing forth — the supreme

children.text: tattvaṃ tat-padam eti vastu paramaṃ vācyaṃ kim atrādhikam // HYP_4.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>tattva</s> (reality), that state he attains — the ultimate reality; what more need be said here? (HYP 4.41)

children.text: divā na pūjayel liṅgaṃ rātrau caiva na pūjayet /
children.translated_text: One should not worship the <s>liṅga</s> only by day, nor should one worship it only by night,

children.text: sarvadā pūjayel liṅgaṃ divārātri-nirodhataḥ // HYP_4.42 //
children.translated_text: one should worship the <s>liṅga</s> always, by transcending day and night. (HYP 4.42)

children.text: atha khecarī-
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Khecarī</s> [Mudrā]:

children.text: savya-dakṣiṇa-nāḍī-stho madhye carati mārutaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the breath, [normally] moving in the left and right <s>nāḍīs</s>, moves in the middle,

children.text: tiṣṭhate khecarī mudrā tasmin sthāne na saṃśayaḥ // HYP_4.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s> is established in that place — there is no doubt. (HYP 4.43)

children.text: iḍā-piṅgalayor madhye śūnyaṃ caivānilaṃ graset /
children.translated_text: In the space between <s>iḍā</s> and <s>piṅgalā</s>, one should absorb the breath in the void,

children.text: tiṣṭhate khecarī mudrā tatra satyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ // HYP_4.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s> is established there — this is truly [repeated] again and again. (HYP 4.44)

children.text: sūrcyācandramasor madhye nirālambāntare punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the space between the sun and moon [channels], in the unsupported interior,

children.text: saṃsthitā vyoma-cakre yā sā mudrā nāma khecarī // HYP_4.45 //
children.translated_text: that which is established in the space-<s>cakra</s> — that <s>mudrā</s> is called <s>Khecarī</s>. (HYP 4.45)

children.text: somād yatroditā dhārā sākṣāt sā śiva-vallabhā /
children.translated_text: Where the stream arising from the moon [flows] — that itself is dear to <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: pūrayed atulāṃ divyāṃ suṣumṇāṃ paścime mukhe // HYP_4.46 //
children.translated_text: one should fill the incomparable, divine <s>suṣumnā</s> at its posterior opening. (HYP 4.46)

children.text: purastāc caiva pūryeta niścitā khecarī bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should fill it from the front as well — then <s>Khecarī</s> is certainly established,

children.text: abhyastā khecarī mudrāpy unmanī samprajāyate // HYP_4.47 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s> is practiced, <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind) fully arises. (HYP 4.47)

children.text: bhruvor madhye śiva-sthānaṃ manas tatra vilīyate /
children.translated_text: Between the eyebrows is the abode of <s>Śiva</s>; there the mind dissolves,

children.text: jñātavyaṃ tat-padaṃ turyaṃ tatra kālo na vidyate // HYP_4.48 //
children.translated_text: that state should be known as <s>turya</s> (the fourth) — there, time does not exist. (HYP 4.48)

children.text: abhyaset khecarīṃ tāvad yāvat syād yoga-nidritaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should practice <s>Khecarī</s> until one attains <s>yoga-nidrā</s> (yogic sleep),

children.text: samprāpta-yoga-nidrasya kālo nāsti kadācana // HYP_4.49 //
children.translated_text: for one who has attained <s>yoga-nidrā</s>, time never exists. (HYP 4.49)

children.text: nirālambaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiṃcid api cintayet /
children.translated_text: Having made the mind supportless, one should not think of anything at all,

children.text: sa-bāhyābhyantaraṃ vyomni ghaṭavat tiṣṭhati dhruvam // HYP_4.50 //
children.translated_text: like a pot in both external and internal space, one remains fixed. (HYP 4.50)

children.text: bāhya-vāyur yathā līnas tathā madhyo na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the external breath is dissolved, so too the middle [breath] — without doubt,

children.text: sva-sthāne sthiratām eti pavano manasā saha // HYP_4.51 //
children.translated_text: the breath, together with the mind, attains steadiness in its own place. (HYP 4.51)

children.text: evam abhyasyatas tasya vāyu-mārge divāniśam /
children.translated_text: Thus, for the one who practices in the path of the breath, day and night,

children.text: abhyāsāj jīryate vāyur manas tatraiva līyate // HYP_4.52 //
children.translated_text: through practice, the breath is dissolved, and the mind dissolves there as well. (HYP 4.52)

children.text: amṛtaiḥ plāvayed deham āpāda-tala-mastakam /
children.translated_text: One should flood the body with nectar from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head,

children.text: siddhyaty eva mahā-kāyo mahā-bala-parākramaḥ // HYP_4.53 //
children.translated_text: a great body with great strength and valor is certainly accomplished. (HYP 4.53)

children.text: śakti-madhye manaḥ kṛtvā śaktiṃ mānasa-madhyagām /
children.translated_text: Placing the mind in the middle of <s>Śakti</s> (power), and <s>Śakti</s> in the middle of the mind,

children.text: manasā mana ālokya dhārayet paramaṃ padam // HYP_4.54 //
children.translated_text: observing the mind with the mind itself, one should fix upon the supreme state. (HYP 4.54)

children.text: kha-madhye kuru cātmānam ātma-madhye ca khaṃ kuru /
children.translated_text: Place the Self in the midst of space, and space in the midst of the Self,

children.text: sarvaṃ ca kha-mayaṃ kṛtvā na kiṃcid api cintayet // HYP_4.55 //
children.translated_text: having made everything pervaded by space, one should not think of anything. (HYP 4.55)

children.text: antaḥ śūnyo bahiḥ śūnyaḥ śūnyaḥ kumbha ivāmbare /
children.translated_text: Empty within, empty without — empty like a pot in the sky,

children.text: antaḥ pūrṇo bahiḥ pūrṇaḥ pūrṇaḥ kumbha ivārṇave // HYP_4.56 //
children.translated_text: full within, full without — full like a pot in the ocean. (HYP 4.56)

children.text: bāhya-cintā na kartavyā tathaivāntara-cintanam /
children.translated_text: One should not engage in external thought, nor likewise in internal thought,

children.text: sarva-cintāṃ parityajya na kiṃcid api cintayet // HYP_4.57 //
children.translated_text: abandoning all thought, one should not think of anything at all. (HYP 4.57)

children.text: saṅkalpa-mātra-kalanaiva jagat samagraṃ
children.translated_text: The entire world is merely the play of thought (<s>saṅkalpa</s>),

children.text: saṅkalpa-mātra-kalanaiva mano-vilāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: the play of the mind is merely the play of thought,

children.text: saṅkalpa-mātra-matim utsṛja nirvikalpam
children.translated_text: abandoning the intellect based merely on thought, and resorting to the thought-free (<s>nirvikalpa</s>),

children.text: āśritya niścayam avāpnuhi rāma śāntim // HYP_4.58 //
children.translated_text: attain certainty and peace, O <s>Rāma</s>! (HYP 4.58)

children.text: karpūram anale yadvat saindhavaṃ salile yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as camphor [dissolves] in fire, and rock salt in water,

children.text: tathā sandhīyamānaṃ ca manas tattve vilīyate // HYP_4.59 //
children.translated_text: so too the mind, when united [with the supreme], dissolves into <s>tattva</s> (reality). (HYP 4.59)

children.text: jñeyaṃ sarvaṃ pratītaṃ ca jñānaṃ ca mana ucyate /
children.translated_text: All that is knowable and all that is perceived, as well as knowledge itself, is called mind,

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ samaṃ naṣṭaṃ nānyaḥ panthā dvitīyakaḥ // HYP_4.60 //
children.translated_text: when knowledge and the knowable are equally destroyed, there is no other, second path. (HYP 4.60)

children.text: mano-dṛśyam idaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiṃcit sa-carācaram /
children.translated_text: All this, whatever is movable and immovable, is the perception of the mind,

children.text: manaso hy unmanī-bhāvād dvaitaṃ naivolabhyate // HYP_4.61 //
children.translated_text: but when the mind attains the state of <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence), duality is no longer found. (HYP 4.61)

children.text: jñeya-vastu-parityāgād vilayaṃ yāti mānasam /
children.translated_text: By the abandonment of all knowable objects, the mind attains dissolution,

children.text: manaso vilaye jāte kaivalyam avaśiṣyate // HYP_4.62 //
children.translated_text: when the mind is dissolved, <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) alone remains. (HYP 4.62)

children.text: evaṃ nānā-vidhopāyāḥ samyak svānubhavānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, various methods, properly accompanied by one's own experience,

children.text: samādhi-mārgāḥ kathitāḥ pūrvācāryair mahātmabhiḥ // HYP_4.63 //
children.translated_text: as paths to <s>samādhi</s>, have been taught by the great-souled earlier teachers. (HYP 4.63)

children.text: suṣumṇāyai kuṇḍalinyai sudhāyai candra-janmane /
children.translated_text: To <s>Suṣumnā</s>, to <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, to the nectar, to the moon-born,

children.text: manonmanyai namas tubhyaṃ mahā-śaktyai cid-ātmane // HYP_4.64 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Manonmanī</s>, to the great <s>Śakti</s>, to the consciousness-Self — salutations to You! (HYP 4.64)

children.text: aśakya-tattva-bodhānāṃ mūḍhānām api saṃmatam /
children.translated_text: Even for the dull, who are incapable of grasping the truth, approved [by all],

children.text: proktaṃ gorakṣa-nāthena nādopāsanam ucyate // HYP_4.65 //
children.translated_text: is the worship of <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) as taught by <s>Gorakṣanātha</s>. (HYP 4.65)

children.text: śrī-ādināthena sa-pāda-koṭi-
children.translated_text: By the revered <s>Ādinātha</s>, one and a quarter crore (12.5 million)

children.text: laya-prakārāḥ kathitā jayanti /
children.translated_text: methods of <s>laya</s> (dissolution) have been declared — they are triumphant,

children.text: nādānusandhānakam ekam eva
children.translated_text: but we consider <s>nādānusandhāna</s> (meditation on the inner sound) alone

children.text: manyāmahe mukhyatamaṃ layānām // HYP_4.66 //
children.translated_text: to be the foremost of all [methods of] <s>laya</s>. (HYP 4.66)

children.text: muktāsane sthito yogī mudrāṃ sandhāya śāmbhavīm /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s>, seated in <s>Muktāsana</s> (liberated posture), performing <s>Śāmbhavī Mudrā</s>,

children.text: śṛṇuyād dakṣiṇe karṇe nādam antāstham ekadhīḥ // HYP_4.67 //
children.translated_text: should listen with single-pointed mind to the inner sound (<s>nāda</s>) in the right ear. (HYP 4.67)

children.text: śravaṇa-puṭa-nayana-yugala-
children.translated_text: The closing of the ears, the pair of eyes,

children.text: ghrāṇa-mukhānāṃ nirodhanaṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text: the nose, and the mouth should be performed,

children.text: śuddha-suṣumṇā-saraṇau
children.translated_text: in the purified path of <s>suṣumnā</s>,

children.text: sphuṭam amalaḥ śrūyate nādaḥ // HYP_4.68 //
children.translated_text: the inner sound (<s>nāda</s>) is clearly heard, pure and stainless. (HYP 4.68)

children.text: ārambhaś ca ghaṭaś caiva tathā paricayo'pi ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Ārambha</s> (beginning), <s>Ghaṭa</s> (vessel), and likewise <s>Paricaya</s> (familiarity),

children.text: niṣpattiḥ sarva-yogeṣu syād avasthā-catuṣṭayam // HYP_4.69 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Niṣpatti</s> (consummation) — in all <s>yogas</s>, there is a fourfold progression of states. (HYP 4.69)

children.text: atha ārambhāvasthā-
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Ārambha</s> (beginning) state:

children.text: brahma-granther bhaved bhedo hy ānandaḥ śūnya-sambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>Brahma granthi</s> (knot of <s>Brahmā</s>) is pierced, bliss arises from the void,

children.text: vicitraḥ kvaṇako dehe'nāhataḥ śrūyate dhvaniḥ // HYP_4.70 //
children.translated_text: wonderful tinkling sounds are heard in the body — the unstruck (<s>anāhata</s>) sound. (HYP 4.70)

children.text: divya-dehaś ca tejasvī divya-gandhas tvarogavān /
children.translated_text: The body becomes divine and radiant, with divine fragrance, and free from disease,

children.text: sampūrṇa-hṛdayaḥ śūnya ārambhe yogavān bhavet // HYP_4.71 //
children.translated_text: with the heart full [yet] empty — in the beginning stage, one becomes a true <s>yogī</s>. (HYP 4.71)

children.text: atha ghaṭāvasthā-
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Ghaṭa</s> (vessel) state:

children.text: dvitīyāyāṃ ghaṭīkṛtya vāyur bhavati madhyagaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the second [stage], the breath, having been united, enters the middle [channel],

children.text: dṛḍhāsano bhaved yogī jñānī deva-samas tadā // HYP_4.72 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> becomes firm in posture, wise, and equal to the gods. (HYP 4.72)

children.text: viṣṇu-granthes tato bhedāt paramānanda-sūcakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, from the piercing of the <s>Viṣṇu granthi</s> (knot of <s>Viṣṇu</s>), indicating supreme bliss,

children.text: atiśūnye vimardaś ca bherī-śabdas tadā bhavet // HYP_4.73 //
children.translated_text: in the great void, a rumbling sound like a kettledrum arises. (HYP 4.73)

children.text: atha paricayāvasthā-
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Paricaya</s> (familiarity) state:

children.text: tṛtīyāyāṃ tu vijñeyo vihāyo mardala-dhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third [stage], the sound of a drum, like [that heard in] the sky, should be known,

children.text: mahā-śūnyaṃ tadā yāti sarva-siddhi-samāśrayam // HYP_4.74 //
children.translated_text: then one reaches the great void, the abode of all accomplishments. (HYP 4.74)

children.text: cittānandaṃ tadā jitvā sahajānanda-sambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having conquered the bliss of the mind, the bliss born of the natural state (<s>sahajānanda</s>) arises,

children.text: doṣa-duḥkha-jarā-vyādhi-kṣudhā-nidrā-vivarjitaḥ // HYP_4.75 //
children.translated_text: free from <s>doṣas</s> (defects), suffering, old age, disease, hunger, and sleep. (HYP 4.75)

children.text: atha niṣpatty-avasthā-
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Niṣpatti</s> (consummation) state:

children.text: rudra-granthiṃ yadā bhittvā śarva-pīṭha-gato'nilaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the <s>Rudra granthi</s> (knot of <s>Rudra</s>) is pierced and the breath reaches the seat of <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: niṣpattau vaiṇavaḥ śabdaḥ kvaṇad-vīṇā-kvaṇo bhavet // HYP_4.76 //
children.translated_text: in the final stage, the sound of a flute and the resonance of a vibrating <s>vīṇā</s> arise. (HYP 4.76)

children.text: ekībhūtaṃ tadā cittaṃ rāja-yogābhidhānakam /
children.translated_text: The mind then becomes unified — this is called <s>Rāja Yoga</s>,

children.text: sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra-kartāsau yogīśvara-samo bhavet // HYP_4.77 //
children.translated_text: he becomes the maker of creation and dissolution, equal to the Lord of <s>yogīs</s>. (HYP 4.77)

children.text: astu vā māstu vā muktir atraivākhaṇḍitaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: Whether there be liberation or not — here there is unbroken bliss,

children.text: layodbhavam idaṃ saukhyaṃ rāja-yogād avāpyate // HYP_4.78 //
children.translated_text: this happiness, born of <s>laya</s> (dissolution), is attained through <s>Rāja Yoga</s>. (HYP 4.78)

children.text: rāja-yogam ajānantaḥ kevalaṃ haṭha-karmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who do not know <s>Rāja Yoga</s> and are merely practitioners of <s>Haṭha</s> practices,

children.text: etān abhyāsino manye prayāsa-phala-varjitān // HYP_4.79 //
children.translated_text: I consider them to be deprived of the fruit of their effort. (HYP 4.79)

children.text: unmany-avāptaye śīghraṃ bhrū-dhyānaṃ mama saṃmatam /
children.translated_text: For the swift attainment of <s>unmanī</s>, meditation between the eyebrows is my recommendation,

children.text: rāja-yoga-padaṃ prāptuṃ sukhopāyo'lpa-cetasām /
children.translated_text: it is an easy means for those of lesser intellect to attain the state of <s>Rāja Yoga</s>,

children.text: sadyaḥ pratyaya-sandhāyī jāyate nādajo layaḥ // HYP_4.80 //
children.translated_text: the <s>laya</s> born of <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) instantly produces conviction. (HYP 4.80)

children.text: nādānusandhāna-samādhi-bhājāṃ
children.translated_text: For the lords of <s>yogīs</s> who are devoted to the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>nāda</s>-meditation,

children.text: yogīśvarāṇāṃ hṛdi vardhamānam /
children.translated_text: the bliss growing in the heart,

children.text: ānandam ekaṃ vacasām agamyaṃ
children.translated_text: that singular [bliss], beyond the reach of words —

children.text: jānāti taṃ śrī-gurunātha ekaḥ // HYP_4.81 //
children.translated_text: only the revered <s>Gurunātha</s> (lord guru) knows it. (HYP 4.81)

children.text: karṇau pidhāya hastābhyāṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti dhvaniṃ muniḥ /
children.translated_text: The sage who, blocking the ears with his hands, listens to the inner sound,

children.text: tatra cittaṃ sthirīkuryād yāvat sthira-padaṃ vrajet // HYP_4.82 //
children.translated_text: should fix his mind there until he attains the immovable state. (HYP 4.82)

children.text: abhyasyamāno nādo'yaṃ bāhyam āvṛṇute dhvanim /
children.translated_text: This <s>nāda</s>, when practiced, drowns out external sounds,

children.text: pakṣād vikṣepam akhilaṃ jitvā yogī sukhī bhavet // HYP_4.83 //
children.translated_text: within a fortnight, having conquered all distraction, the <s>yogī</s> becomes blissful. (HYP 4.83)

children.text: śrūyate prathamābhyāse nādo nānā-vidho mahān /
children.translated_text: In the initial practice, the <s>nāda</s> is heard in many great forms,

children.text: tato'bhyāse vardhamāne śrūyate sūkṣma-sūkṣmakaḥ // HYP_4.84 //
children.translated_text: as the practice increases, it is heard in increasingly subtle forms. (HYP 4.84)

children.text: ādau jaladhi-jīmūta-bherī-jharjhara-sambhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: At first, sounds arise like those of the ocean, thundercloud, kettledrum, and waterfall,

children.text: madhye mardala-śaṅkhotthā ghaṇṭā-kāhalajās tathā // HYP_4.85 //
children.translated_text: in the middle, like those of a drum, conch, bell, and horn. (HYP 4.85)

children.text: ante tu kiṅkiṇī-vaṃśa-vīṇā-bhramara-niḥsvanāḥ /
children.translated_text: At the end, sounds like small bells, bamboo flute, <s>vīṇā</s>, and bees,

children.text: iti nānāvidhā nādāḥ śrūyante deha-madhyagāḥ // HYP_4.86 //
children.translated_text: thus, various sounds are heard arising from the middle of the body. (HYP 4.86)

children.text: mahati śrūyamāṇe'pi megha-bhery-ādike dhvanau /
children.translated_text: Even when the great sounds like thunder and kettledrum are heard,

children.text: tatra sūkṣmāt sūkṣmataraṃ nādam eva parāmṛśet // HYP_4.87 //
children.translated_text: one should attend only to the subtler and subtler <s>nāda</s>. (HYP 4.87)

children.text: ghanam utsṛjya vā sūkṣme sūkṣmam utsṛjya vā ghane /
children.translated_text: Whether leaving the gross for the subtle, or leaving the subtle for the gross,

children.text: ramamāṇam api kṣiptaṃ mano nānyatra cālayet // HYP_4.88 //
children.translated_text: the mind, though delighting [in sounds], once engaged, should not be moved elsewhere. (HYP 4.88)

children.text: yatra kutrāpi vā nāde lagati prathamaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wherever the mind first attaches itself to any <s>nāda</s>,

children.text: tatraiva susthirībhūya tena sārdhaṃ vilīyate // HYP_4.89 //
children.translated_text: there itself it becomes firmly established and dissolves along with it. (HYP 4.89)

children.text: makarandaṃ piban bhṛṅgī gandhaṃ nāpekṣate yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a bee drinking nectar does not care for the fragrance,

children.text: nādāsaktaṃ tathā cittaṃ viṣayān nahi kāṅkṣate // HYP_4.90 //
children.translated_text: so the mind attached to <s>nāda</s> does not desire sense-objects. (HYP 4.90)

children.text: mano-matta-gajendrasya viṣayodyāna-cāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the intoxicated elephant of the mind, roaming in the garden of sense-objects,

children.text: samartho'yaṃ niyamane nināda-niśitāṅkuśaḥ // HYP_4.91 //
children.translated_text: this sharp goad of <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) is capable of restraining it. (HYP 4.91)

children.text: baddhaṃ tu nāda-bandhena manaḥ santyakta-cāpalam /
children.translated_text: The mind, bound by the bond of <s>nāda</s>, having abandoned its restlessness,

children.text: prayāti sutarāṃ sthairyaṃ chinna-pakṣaḥ khago yathā // HYP_4.92 //
children.translated_text: attains supreme steadiness — like a bird with clipped wings. (HYP 4.92)

children.text: sarva-cintāṃ parityajya sāvadhānena cetasā /
children.translated_text: Abandoning all thoughts, with an attentive mind,

children.text: nāda evānusandheyo yoga-sāmrājyam icchatā // HYP_4.93 //
children.translated_text: one desiring the sovereignty of <s>yoga</s> should meditate solely on <s>nāda</s>. (HYP 4.93)

children.text: nādo'ntaraṅga-sāraṅga-bandhane vāgurāyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Nāda</s> is like a snare for capturing the inner deer [of the mind],

children.text: antaraṅga-kuraṅgasya vadhe vyādhāyate'pi ca // HYP_4.94 //
children.translated_text: and also like a hunter for slaying the inner deer. (HYP 4.94)

children.text: antaraṅgasya yamino vājinaḥ parighāyate /
children.translated_text: It is like a bolt for restraining the inner horse of the disciplined one,

children.text: nādopāsti-rato nityam avadhāryā hi yoginā // HYP_4.95 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> should always be devoted to the practice of <s>nāda</s>. (HYP 4.95)

children.text: baddhaṃ vimukta-cāñcalyaṃ nāda-gandhaka-jāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: The mercury of the mind, bound and freed from its restlessness through the alchemy of <s>nāda</s>,

children.text: manaḥ-pāradam āpnoti nirālambākhya-khe'ṭanam // HYP_4.96 //
children.translated_text: attains roaming in the space called 'supportless' (<s>nirālamba</s>). (HYP 4.96)

children.text: nāda-śravaṇataḥ kṣipram antaraṅga-bhujaṅgamam /
children.translated_text: From hearing <s>nāda</s>, the inner serpent [of the mind]

children.text: vismṛtaya sarvam ekāgraḥ kutracin nahi dhāvati // HYP_4.97 //
children.translated_text: quickly forgets everything, and, single-pointed, does not run anywhere. (HYP 4.97)

children.text: kāṣṭhe pravartito vahniḥ kāṣṭhena saha śāmyati /
children.translated_text: Fire kindled in wood is extinguished along with the wood,

children.text: nāde pravartitaṃ cittaṃ nādena saha līyate // HYP_4.98 //
children.translated_text: the mind set in motion by <s>nāda</s> dissolves along with <s>nāda</s>. (HYP 4.98)

children.text: ghaṇṭādināda-sakta-stabdhāntaḥ-karaṇa-hariṇasya /
children.translated_text: For the deer of the inner sense, made motionless by being attached to sounds like bells and so forth,

children.text: praharaṇam api sukaraṃ syāc chara-sandhāna-pravīṇaś cet // HYP_4.99 //
children.translated_text: even the killing [of it] would be easy, if one is skilled in aiming the arrow. (HYP 4.99)

children.text: anāhatasya śabdasya dhvanir ya upalabhyate /
children.translated_text: The resonance that is perceived of the unstruck sound (<s>anāhata śabda</s>),

children.text: dhvaner antargataṃ jñeyaṃ jñeyasyāntargataṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: the knowable is within that resonance, and the mind is within that knowable,

children.text: manas tatra layaṃ yāti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // HYP_4.100 //
children.translated_text: the mind dissolves there — that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (HYP 4.100)

children.text: tāvad ākāśa-saṅkalpo yāvac chabdaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: The concept of space persists as long as sound continues,

children.text: niḥśabdaṃ tat-paraṃ brahma paramāteti gīyate // HYP_4.101 //
children.translated_text: the soundless — that supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme Self — is celebrated. (HYP 4.101)

children.text: yat kiṃcin nāda-rūpeṇa śrūyate śaktir eva sā /
children.translated_text: Whatever is heard in the form of <s>nāda</s> — that is <s>Śakti</s> (power) alone,

children.text: yas tattvānto nirākāraḥ sa eva parameśvaraḥ // HYP_4.102 //
children.translated_text: that which is the end of all principles, formless — that alone is the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). (HYP 4.102)

children.text: sarve haṭha-layopāyā rājayogasya siddhaye /
children.translated_text: All the methods of <s>Haṭha</s> and <s>laya</s> are for the accomplishment of <s>Rāja Yoga</s>,

children.text: rāja-yoga-samārūḍhaḥ puruṣaḥ kāla-vañcakaḥ // HYP_4.103 //
children.translated_text: the person who has ascended to <s>Rāja Yoga</s> is a deceiver of death. (HYP 4.103)

children.text: tattvaṃ bījaṃ haṭhaḥ kṣetram audāsīnyaṃ jalaṃ tribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Tattva</s> (truth) is the seed, <s>Haṭha</s> is the field, detachment (<s>audāsīnya</s>) is the water — by these three,

children.text: unmanī kalpa-latikā sadya eva pravartate // HYP_4.104 //
children.translated_text: the wish-fulfilling creeper of <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind) immediately grows. (HYP 4.104)

children.text: sadā nādānusandhānāt kṣīyante pāpa-saṃcayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through constant meditation on <s>nāda</s>, the accumulations of sin are destroyed,

children.text: nirañjane vilīyete niścitaṃ citta-mārutau // HYP_4.105 //
children.translated_text: the mind and breath certainly dissolve in the stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>) [Absolute]. (HYP 4.105)

children.text: śaṅkha-dundhubhi-nādaṃ ca na śṛṇoti kadācana /
children.translated_text: He no longer hears the sounds of conch or kettledrum,

children.text: kāṣṭhavaj jāyate deha unmanyāvasthayā dhruvam // HYP_4.106 //
children.translated_text: the body becomes like a log of wood in the state of <s>unmanī</s>, assuredly. (HYP 4.106)

children.text: sarvāvasthā-vinirmuktaḥ sarva-cintā-vivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Freed from all states, devoid of all thought,

children.text: mṛtavat tiṣṭhate yogī sa mukto nātra saṃśayaḥ // HYP_4.107 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> remains like one dead — he is liberated, without doubt. (HYP 4.107)

children.text: khādyate na ca kālena bādhyate na ca karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: He is not consumed by time, nor bound by <s>karma</s> —

children.text: sādhyate na sa kenāpi yogī yuktaḥ samādhinā // HYP_4.108 //
children.translated_text: Cannot be attained by anyone — the <s>yogī</s> united with <s>samādhi</s>. // HYP 4.108 //

children.text: na gandhaṃ na rasaṃ rūpaṃ na ca sparśaṃ na niḥsvanam /
children.translated_text: He perceives no smell, no taste, no form, no touch, no sound,

children.text: nātmānaṃ na paraṃ vetti yogī yuktaḥ samādhinā // HYP_4.109 //
children.translated_text: Nor himself, nor another — the <s>yogī</s> united with <s>samādhi</s>. // HYP 4.109 //

children.text: cittaṃ na suptaṃ nojāgrat smṛti-vismṛti-varjitam /
children.translated_text: The mind is neither asleep nor awake, free from remembering and forgetting,

children.text: na cāstam eti nodeti yasyāsau mukta eva saḥ // HYP_4.110 //
children.translated_text: It neither sets nor rises — he whose [mind is thus] is indeed liberated. // HYP 4.110 //

children.text: na vijānāti śītoṣṇaṃ na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: He does not perceive cold or heat, neither pain nor pleasure,

children.text: na mānaṃ nopamānaṃ ca yogī yuktaḥ samādhinā // HYP_4.111 //
children.translated_text: Neither honor nor dishonor — the <s>yogī</s> united with <s>samādhi</s>. // HYP 4.111 //

children.text: svastho jāgrad avasthāyāṃ suptavad yo'vatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: One who, though healthy, in the waking state abides as if asleep,

children.text: niḥśvāsocchvāsa-hīnaś ca niścitaṃ mukta eva saḥ // HYP_4.112 //
children.translated_text: Devoid of inhalation and exhalation — he is certainly liberated. // HYP 4.112 //

children.text: avadhyaḥ sarva-śastrāṇām aśakyaḥ sarva-dehinām /
children.translated_text: Invulnerable to all weapons, beyond the power of all beings,

children.text: agrāhyo mantra-yantrāṇāṃ yogī yuktaḥ samādhinā // HYP_4.113 //
children.translated_text: Ungraspable by <s>mantras</s> and <s>yantras</s> — the <s>yogī</s> united with <s>samādhi</s>. // HYP 4.113 //

children.text: yāvan naiva praviśati caran māruto madhya-mārge
children.translated_text: As long as the moving breath does not enter the central channel (<s>madhya-mārga</s>),

children.text: yāvad vidur na bhavati dṛḍhaḥ prāṇa-vāta-prabandhāt /
children.translated_text: As long as <s>bindu</s> (seminal energy) does not become steady through the restraint of the <s>prāṇa</s> breath,

children.text: yāvad dhyāne sahaja-sadṛśaṃ jāyate naiva tattvaṃ
children.translated_text: As long as the reality naturally arising does not manifest in meditation,

children.text: tāvaj jñānaṃ vadati tad idaṃ dambha-mithyā-pralāpaḥ // HYP_4.114 //
children.translated_text: So long, all talk of knowledge is nothing but the babble of deceit and falsehood. // HYP 4.114 //

body.translated_text:
Thus [ends] the description of the characteristics of <s>samādhi</s> in the <s>Haṭha-yoga-pradīpikā</s>,
the Fourth Instruction.
